# 3D Brand in a Box — Low-Noise Apple Park Preview Template

> Fidelity is locked. Enhancement is a separate, explicit request after acceptance.

## Unanimous structural invariants

1. Square, front-facing clear acrylic display box with a shallow elevated view, dark studio field, and a deep branded pedestal. (4/4 previews)
2. A layered miniature branded environment fills the box and places the brand product, UI, or icon at the visual center. (4/4 previews)
3. Brand accent color connects the top rim, internal illuminated sign system, and large pedestal identity zone. (4/4 previews)

## Discriminative signatures

### Believable edited micro-city diorama construction: two calm terraces, sparse scaled figures, selective landscaping, one circulation path, and clear hero breathing room.
- Evidence: preview-01.png, preview-02.png, preview-03.png, preview-04.png (4/4 previews)
- Discriminative weight: 5/5
- Prompt clause: build the scene as a believable hand-crafted micro-city diorama with two calm terraces, no more than eight tiny scaled figures, selective landscaping, one clear circulation path, and generous breathing room around the hero
- Medium/process/substrate: photorealistic miniature-diorama product photography · layered scale-model set construction behind clear acrylic · clear acrylic vitrines, matte-black molded pedestal, miniature architectural materials
- Irregularity: purposeful
- Composition exception: The terrain and building type may change to match the brand subject, but cap the scene at four architectural masses and one circulation path.

### Warm practical miniature lighting contrasts with a dark graphite background and the brand-colored emissive system.
- Evidence: preview-01.png, preview-02.png, preview-03.png, preview-04.png (4/4 previews)
- Discriminative weight: 5/5
- Prompt clause: light the miniature with warm practical window and street lights, restrained brand-colored emissive accents, dark graphite shadows, physically plausible acrylic reflections, and a single grounded contact shadow
- Medium/process/substrate: studio product photography · practical miniature lighting and controlled studio reflections · dark tabletop, clear acrylic, brushed or matte pedestal surfaces
- Irregularity: not marked purposeful
- Composition exception: A bright sky or background may appear only inside a contained brand panel, never as the surrounding studio field.

### At most two physical product or UI boards operate as calm display elements within the diorama, never as flat overlays.
- Evidence: preview-01.png, preview-02.png, preview-03.png, preview-04.png (4/4 previews)
- Discriminative weight: 4/5
- Prompt clause: integrate no more than two clean, physically mounted product or UI display boards into the miniature; keep all visible copy short, large, literal, and limited to a single word per board
- Medium/process/substrate: branded retail-display miniature · physical signboards and product panels staged as model-set elements · lit acrylic signage and dark framed panels
- Irregularity: not marked purposeful
- Composition exception: For a physical product brand, product packaging may replace one board; the second board may be omitted.

## Variable slots

| Slot | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---:|---|---|
| `{BRAND_SUBJECT}` | brand product, service, or software identity | yes | specialty coffee brand with a signature espresso machine | Bind the changing hero to this slot; use a real identity only when the requester supplies or authorizes it. |
| `{BRAND_NAME}` | short literal brand name | yes | NORTHLINE COFFEE | Use a short all-caps or title-case mark on the pedestal; avoid invented extra words. |
| `{TAGLINE}` | short literal tagline | yes | Small batch. Big city. | Limit to six words for legibility. |
| `{ACCENT_COLOR}` | named brand accent color | yes | copper orange | Use one accent color plus neutrals; do not introduce a rainbow palette. |

## Model-prior hazards

- **Uncontrolled micro-detail accumulation** — likely failure: The miniature turns into visual noise with duplicate objects, stray lights, malformed people, and unreadable labels.; countermeasure: Limit the scene to one dominant hero, two display boards maximum, four architectural masses, eight figures maximum, one circulation path, broad readable shapes, and three quiet visual zones at thumbnail scale.
- **Fake brand copy and pseudo-UI** — likely failure: The model fills panels with gibberish, logos, or tiny controls that undermine a usable advertisement.; countermeasure: Use only the supplied literal BRAND_NAME and TAGLINE; make interface display boards graphic and text-sparse, with no microtext or invented marks.
- **Synthetic acrylic and floating set pieces** — likely failure: Glass edges melt, reflections conflict, and miniature buildings or products appear to float.; countermeasure: Specify crisp acrylic corner seams, restrained physically plausible reflections, clear scale-model joints, and one consistent contact-shadow direction.

## Fidelity-locked prompt skeleton

Create a premium 1:1 3D brand advertisement for {BRAND_SUBJECT}. Compose a square front-facing clear acrylic display box on a deep matte-black branded pedestal, photographed from a shallow elevated view against a near-black studio background. A layered miniature branded environment fills the box, with one dominant product, interface, or brand icon as the visual center. Use the brand accent color consistently on the top rim, restrained internal illuminated signs, and the pedestal identity zone. Build the scene as a believable hand-crafted micro-city diorama with two calm terraces, no more than eight tiny scaled figures, selective landscaping, one clear circulation path, and generous breathing room around the hero. Integrate no more than two clean, physically mounted product or UI display boards into the miniature; keep all visible copy short, large, literal, and limited to a single word per board. Light the miniature with warm practical window and street lights, restrained brand-colored emissive accents, dark graphite shadows, physically plausible acrylic reflections, and a single grounded contact shadow. Use {ACCENT_COLOR} as the only saturated accent. Put the exact literal brand name {BRAND_NAME} large and clean on the front pedestal, and the exact literal tagline {TAGLINE} once as a secondary line. Keep the hero object count to one, every miniature object structurally coherent and intentionally placed, with four architectural masses maximum, three quiet visual zones, and uncluttered negative space around the pedestal copy. Do not add watermarks, signatures, extra logos, fake small text, duplicate objects, floating elements, distorted acrylic, extraneous decorative clutter, dense crowds, repeated signage, or decorative filler.

## Optional enhancement boundary

Do not improve, polish, modernize, or reinterpret this skeleton during cloning or ordinary use. After a fidelity-passing render exists, an explicit user request may authorize a separate enhancement variant; keep the accepted fidelity-locked skeleton unchanged.

presets.template:
# Branded IV Drip Art — template

Triangulated from 9 source previews. Refined with the vault's gpt-image-2 prompting techniques:

- **json-spec hyperrealism format** (Pass 6 of `template-extraction-rubric.md`) — the strongest register for tight micro-detail product shots.
- **Layout-as-prompt for the surface print** — brand wordmark, logo and tagline are pinned to explicit zones on the bag.
- **Style-deviation tail clause** — `photoreal product photography, not illustrated, not cartoon, not glossy CGI` deflects the model away from the default cartoon-glossy fallback.
- **Render-text-verbatim guard** — explicit instruction that brand wordmark and tagline must render letter-for-letter as supplied, which is the most common failure mode on gpt-image-2 brand-logo work.

## Invariants

Always-on properties of every generation from this skill:

1. Square 1:1 composition (1024x1024).
2. Transparent medical IV drip bag — clear flexible medical-grade PVC, sealed seams, rounded corners, vertical rectangular pouch with roughly 3:4 internal proportions.
3. Thin black metal S-hook hanging the bag from a single point at the top.
4. Drip-chamber and luer-lock port at the bottom, with a translucent silicone IV tube descending and tinted by the liquid.
5. Liquid fills about 80% of the bag, color matches the brand's signature palette, with believable meniscus.
6. Brand logo printed crisply on the upper-mid bag face, brand wordmark with it, ironic parody tagline directly below.
7. Off-white / neutral light-gray seamless studio cyc background with soft falloff.
8. Subtle drop shadow behind and to the right of the bag.
9. Soft top-down softbox lighting, subtle highlight along the bag's left curved edge, realistic glossy reflections on the plastic.
10. Hyperrealistic 3D product-photography render, sharp focus on the bag.

## Variable slots

| Slot | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `BRAND_NAME` | string, 1-3 words | yes | Brand wordmark to print on the bag. |
| `BRAND_LOGO` | string, descriptive phrase | yes | Logo/emblem description, centered upper-mid on the bag. Be specific: shape, primary color, any distinctive feature. |
| `LIQUID_COLOR` | named or hex color | yes | Beverage fill color matching the brand identity. Include translucency note. |
| `TAGLINE` | 2-5 words, all caps | yes | Ironic parody of the brand's real slogan with medical/needle/vein irony. |
| `DRINK_TEXTURE` | enum | no | One of: `ice cubes`, `carbonation bubbles`, `boba pearls`, `foam head`, `condensation droplets`, `smooth liquid`. Default `smooth liquid`. |

## Prompt skeleton

Feed this verbatim to `image-gen-cli` after replacing every `{SLOT}` token. Format: json-spec.

```json
{
  "task": "Render a hyperrealistic 3D product photograph as a 1024x1024 square image.",
  "aspect_ratio": "1:1",
  "subject": {
    "object": "transparent medical IV drip bag",
    "material": "clear flexible medical-grade PVC with realistic plastic thickness, refraction, molded seams, sealed edges, subtle wrinkles, rounded corners, and a vertical rectangular pouch with approximately 3:4 internal proportions",
    "hardware": "thin black metal S-hook at the top through the hanging slot; drip-chamber and luer-lock port at the bottom; translucent silicone IV tube descending from the port and tinted by the liquid",
    "framing": "front-facing centered hero product composition, bag filling most of the frame"
  },
  "liquid_fill": {
    "color": "{LIQUID_COLOR}",
    "fill_level": "about 80% full",
    "texture": "{DRINK_TEXTURE}",
    "detail": "transparent beverage volume visible through the bag, with believable meniscus and liquid tint carried into the tube"
  },
  "surface_print": {
    "logo": "{BRAND_LOGO}",
    "brand_wordmark": "{BRAND_NAME}",
    "tagline": "{TAGLINE}",
    "placement": "logo centered upper-mid on the IV bag, brand wordmark integrated with the logo, tagline directly below the logo as a separate bold sans-serif line",
    "print_quality": "brand's actual typeface, crisply screen-printed onto the bag's plastic surface; sharp edges, no warping, no distortion across plastic folds or curvature",
    "text_fidelity": "the brand wordmark must read letter-for-letter exactly as: {BRAND_NAME}. The tagline must read letter-for-letter exactly as: {TAGLINE}. Do not paraphrase, abbreviate, or substitute characters."
  },
  "background": "seamless off-white / neutral light-gray studio cyc with soft falloff and a subtle drop shadow behind and slightly to the right of the bag",
  "lighting": "soft top-down softbox key light, subtle highlight along the bag's left curved edge, gentle gradient on the plastic, realistic glossy reflections, no harsh specular hotspots",
  "camera": "sharp focus on the bag, shallow depth of field falloff at edges, high-end studio product photography perspective, eye-level slightly above center",
  "style": "photoreal product photography, not illustrated, not cartoon, not glossy CGI — read like a real high-end studio product shot of a real promotional IV-pouch novelty",
  "negative": "no juice pouch, no smoothie packet, no Capri-Sun shape, no toy bag, no wavy text, no misspelled wordmarks, no extra hardware, no medical room background, no patient, no syringe, no needle visible above the hook"
}
```

## Failure-mode reruns

If the first generation fails any of these, regenerate with the listed adjustment appended as a tail clause:

- **Wordmark misspelled or warped** → append `the wordmark "{BRAND_NAME}" is rendered letter-for-letter exactly as: {BRAND_NAME}. Do not warp.`
- **Bag reads as a juice pouch / Capri-Sun** → append `the bag is a clinical hospital-grade IV drip bag like the ones used in hospitals, with a hard luer-lock port and visible drip-chamber, not a juice pouch and not a smoothie bag.`
- **Liquid color too saturated / cartoony** → append `the liquid color is exactly {LIQUID_COLOR}, with realistic transparency and slight darkening at the bottom from beverage volume.`
- **Tagline distorted across folds** → append `the tagline "{TAGLINE}" is on a flat un-creased section of the bag surface, perfectly readable.`
- **Background goes medical-room** → append `the background is a clean off-white studio cyc, not a hospital, not a clinic, no instruments, no people.`

presets.template:
# Prompt Skeleton — Discipline Pill Pack Mockup

This is the canonical prompt skeleton. Fill the `{SLOTS}` from user input. Keep the **invariant block** verbatim — it is the contract that makes the output match the Promptbase template.

---

## Slot list

Required:

- `{BRAND}` — 1-2 word brand mark printed at top of card
- `{PRODUCT_NAME}` — 1-3 word product name (the virtue/concept), large dominant text
- `{DOSAGE_LINE}` — 3-7 word ironic medical descriptor under product name
- `{QUANTITY_BADGE}` — pharma-style quantity copy, e.g. `10 capsules`, `10 doses`, `10 reps` — must match `{CELL_COUNT}` numerically
- `{CELL_COUNT}` — integer (default 10)
- `{GRID_SHAPE}` — `2 rows × 5 columns` (default), `2×4`, `2×6`, `3×5`
- `{OBJECT_INVENTORY}` — the symbolic miniature object(s) inside each cell. One consistent object preferred. If a rotation, name each and assign to specific cells.
- `{DOMINANT_COLOR}` — single brand color of the cardboard backing (named, e.g. `muted slate gray`, `deep navy`)
- `{ACCENT_COLOR}` — single accent color used for the brand glyph, accent stripe, or product-name highlight
- `{BACKDROP}` — surface and backdrop tone (e.g. `soft warm off-white tabletop, seamless paper backdrop in matching warm beige`)

Optional:

- `{ANGLE}` — `front-on` (default) or `shallow 3/4 hero, camera ~15° above horizontal`
- `{FOIL}` — `silver` (default), `gold`, `white`, or color-matched to `{DOMINANT_COLOR}`
- `{ASPECT}` — passed to the backend; default `1024x1024`
- `{EXTRA_FLAVOR}` — small tertiary copy on the card (e.g. `Net Wt. 0.4 oz`, `Rx only`, `USP`, batch number) — keep tiny

---

## Final prompt template

> Conceptual pharmaceutical blister-pack product mockup, single pack, centered, occupying 60-75% of the frame, {ANGLE}, sitting flat on a {BACKDROP} with one soft natural contact shadow under the lower edge.
>
> The pack is a rectangular printed cardboard backing card with rounded corners in matte {DOMINANT_COLOR}, with a regular grid of {GRID_SHAPE} = {CELL_COUNT} clear thermoformed plastic blister domes on the front face, each cell uniform in size and spacing. A thin {FOIL} foil seal layer is visible behind the domes where the cardboard ends.
>
> Each blister cell contains a tiny photoreal miniature {OBJECT_INVENTORY}, scaled to fit, rendered as if physically trapped under the clear dome — visible refraction at the dome edge, a faint plastic specular highlight on top of each dome, a soft contact shadow of the object on the foil layer below. NOT pills. The object is the same in every cell unless otherwise specified.
>
> Printed on the cardboard front face, in this exact stack:
>   1. Brand mark **{BRAND}** at the top, small, simple sans-serif word-mark, accent color {ACCENT_COLOR}.
>   2. Product name **{PRODUCT_NAME}** large and dominant, centered, in bold display type.
>   3. Dosage / descriptor line "**{DOSAGE_LINE}**" directly under the product name, smaller, regular weight.
>   4. Quantity badge "**{QUANTITY_BADGE}**" in a small block at the bottom corner of the card. The number in this badge MUST match the {CELL_COUNT} visible cells.
>   {EXTRA_FLAVOR_LINE_IF_PRESENT}
>
> Color system: one dominant color ({DOMINANT_COLOR}) on the cardboard, one accent ({ACCENT_COLOR}) on the brand mark and a thin accent stripe or underline. Foil is {FOIL}. Domes are crystal clear, slightly glossy, with a soft top highlight.
>
> Lighting: soft top-left key light, large source, low contrast, clean studio fidelity. No hard rim light, no lens flare, no bokeh, no extra props, no hands, no second pack, no exploded view.
>
> Style: high-end conceptual product photography, ironic wellness / pharma satire, modern minimal layout, sharp focus across the entire pack, photoreal.
>
> Spelling must be exact for {BRAND}, {PRODUCT_NAME}, {DOSAGE_LINE}, and {QUANTITY_BADGE}. No additional text anywhere in the image. No watermark, no QR code, no barcode, no seller signature.

---

## Notes on filling slots

- **One object per cell, repeated.** That is the canonical Promptbase look. Use a rotating set only when the user explicitly wants it (e.g., "alarm clock, dumbbell, broccoli, book, water drop" repeating across the row).
- **Quantity badge math.** Always re-check that the badge integer equals `{CELL_COUNT}`. The most common output failure is "10 capsules" printed on a pack with 8 visible cells.
- **Color discipline.** One dominant + one accent. Three or more colors break the look. Foil is its own neutral, it does not count as a third color.
- **Dosage line tone.** Dry, ironic, medical-style cadence. Examples: *one rep, twice daily*, *take before doomscrolling*, *for chronic procrastination*, *non-habit forming, sadly*, *side effects may include progress*. See `concepts.md` for theme-specific dosage lines.
- **Type family.** Bold sans (Helvetica/Inter/Neue Haas) for fitness/utility/discipline. Condensed serif (Canela/Domaine) for "luxury wellness" or skincare-coded. Rounded geometric (DM Sans/Avenir Next Rounded) for soft self-care, sleep, mindfulness.
- **Do not add an `@promptstudio` style watermark.** The Promptbase previews carry one — it is the seller's signature, not part of the template.

If the user gives only a vague vibe ("make me a discipline thing"), propose 2-3 candidate themes and the object inventory you would put in each (drawn from `references/concepts.md`) before generating.

If the user provides a **product/object photo as a reference**, label it explicitly as a `subject reference` (silhouette, color, scale guidance only — the mockup is generated fresh, not edited on top of the photo). # Vacuum-Sealed Gel Logo Packaging Template

> Fidelity is locked. Enhancement is a separate, explicit request after acceptance.

## Unanimous structural invariants

1. A single colored gel emblem is shown frontally inside a clear rectangular vacuum-sealed pouch on a white studio ground. (6/6 previews)
2. The emblem is centered and fully legible, while the pouch carries soft studio shadow and generous pale negative space. (6/6 previews)
3. Compact industrial archive labels and barcode geometry anchor the packaging corners without competing with the hero. (6/6 previews)

## Discriminative signatures

### The hero has transparent, colored gel depth with a crisp outer rim, internal bubbles, and coherent wet-looking refraction.
- Evidence: preview-01.png, preview-02.png, preview-03.png, preview-04.png, preview-05.png, preview-06.png (6/6 previews)
- Discriminative weight: 5/5
- Prompt clause: gel emblem with its defining silhouette and proportions preserved
- Medium/process/substrate: Photorealistic CGI product photograph · Layered translucent gel casting with a clear outer rim and embedded microbubbles · Clear flexible plastic pouch enclosing a translucent gel emblem
- Irregularity: not marked purposeful
- Composition exception: Long horizontal emblems may fill more of the pouch width, while compact emblems retain the same centered pouch treatment.

### The clear pouch surface visibly responds to vacuum pressure through heat seals, pressure wrinkles, trapped air, moisture beads, and slight unevenness.
- Evidence: preview-01.png, preview-02.png, preview-03.png, preview-04.png, preview-05.png, preview-06.png (6/6 previews)
- Discriminative weight: 5/5
- Prompt clause: visible heat-sealed edges, shrink-wrap wrinkles, pressure folds, trapped air bubbles, and scattered condensation droplets
- Medium/process/substrate: Photorealistic CGI product photograph · Vacuum-pack film deformation and condensation simulation · Transparent heat-sealed flexible plastic film
- Irregularity: purposeful
- Composition exception: Wrinkles and droplets may cluster near the emblem or pouch seams, but must not block the emblem silhouette.

### The look combines sparse collectible-industrial archival labeling with a white studio presentation rather than a branded retail carton.
- Evidence: preview-01.png, preview-02.png, preview-03.png, preview-04.png, preview-05.png, preview-06.png (6/6 previews)
- Discriminative weight: 4/5
- Prompt clause: label treatment is compact black sans-serif microcopy and barcode geometry, without invented decorative marks
- Medium/process/substrate: Industrial archive product photography · Applied matte inventory labels and barcode stickers on clear pouch film · White pressure-sensitive paper labels on transparent flexible plastic
- Irregularity: not marked purposeful
- Composition exception: A small fragile or edition mark may use another corner if the emblem's silhouette requires the lower-right area.

## Variable slots

| Slot | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---:|---|---|
| `{SUBJECT}` | brand emblem or original mark | yes | a rounded four-point navigation-star emblem | The one physical emblem inside the pouch; describe its visible silhouette rather than adding a second hero. |

presets.template:
# Vacuum-Sealed Objects Template

Source: Promptbase listing "Vacuumsealed Objects" by @ikuba (https://promptbase.com/prompt/vacuumsealed-objects-2). Prompt was visible on the listing; previews triangulated across 9 source images.

## Required invariants (verbatim — reproduce in every prompt)

1. 2:3 portrait card. Output size 1024×1536 px.
2. Exactly one hero subject, centered, occupying ~60-70% of frame height.
3. Hero fully enclosed inside a transparent crinkled plastic vacuum bag clinging tight to the silhouette.
4. Plastic wrinkles radiate from pressure points; subtle moisture condensation at compression points; specular highlights along wrinkle ridges.
5. Hero silhouette stays clean and legible through the compression and refraction of the plastic.
6. Background: plain soft gray studio backdrop with subtle gradient (or `{BACKGROUND}` override). Soft top-down drop shadow under the bag.
7. Lighting per `{LIGHTING_MOOD}`, default moody top-down studio key with cool ambient fill.
8. Optional adhesive sticker label at bottom-left or bottom-right of the bag carrying `{BRANDING_ELEMENTS}`. White or off-white rectangular sticker, bold industrial sans-serif, 1-2 short lines, optional barcode or edition mark.
9. No watermark, no seller signature, no model badge, no UI chrome.
10. Text accuracy: every word in `{BRANDING_ELEMENTS}` is rendered verbatim.

## Variable slots

| Slot | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `{OBJECT_SEALED}` | string | — | required; one object only |
| `{OBJECT_CHARACTERISTICS}` | string | "clean strong silhouette with material-accurate surface detail" | optional silhouette/material clause |
| `{PLASTIC_TYPE}` | enum | `transparent polyethylene` | also: `frosted vacuum pouch`, `clear poly mailer`, `archival mylar` |
| `{BRANDING_ELEMENTS}` | string | `LIMITED EDITION / 010/100` on a small white adhesive sticker, bottom-right of bag | 1-2 lines, verbatim copy |
| `{LIGHTING_MOOD}` | string | `moody top-down studio key with cool ambient fill` | also: `cinematic side-rim`, `soft overcast`, `warm tungsten edge` |
| `{BACKGROUND}` | string | `plain soft gray studio backdrop with subtle gradient` | also: `off-white seamless`, `cool concrete`, `charcoal void` |

## Prompt skeleton

```
Hyper-realistic high-resolution product render of {OBJECT_SEALED}, fully enclosed inside a vacuum-sealed crinkled bag of {PLASTIC_TYPE} clinging tightly to the object so every contour and surface detail reads through the wrap. {OBJECT_CHARACTERISTICS}; the silhouette stays strong and legible through the compression. Subtle moisture condensation and fine wrinkles radiate from the pressure points, with specular highlights along the wrinkle ridges for tactile realism. A small white adhesive sticker label anchored at the bottom of the bag carries the verbatim copy "{BRANDING_ELEMENTS}" in bold industrial sans-serif, suggesting collectible, archival, or limited-edition status. {BACKGROUND} ensures the plastic tension, reflections, and refractive distortions become the visual focus, with a soft top-down drop shadow grounding the bag. {LIGHTING_MOOD} highlights texture, structure, and material properties for dimensional depth. Composition delivers a product-showcase aesthetic with a moody, edgy, post-consumer collectible undertone. 4K ultra-detailed resolution, photorealistic material physics, award-winning contemporary product photography, sophisticated lighting and reflection work. 2:3 vertical portrait, 1024×1536. No watermark, no seller signature, no model badge, no QR code unless explicitly listed in the branding copy.
```

## Negative guardrails (apply when retrying)

- "single hero object only, no companions, no fragments"
- "plastic must cling to the contour, no loose air pockets larger than a thumbprint"
- "label text reads exactly as quoted, no extra words, no extra lines"
- "no human hands, no faces in the bag, no living subjects sealed inside plastic"
- "no QR code, no barcode" (only if user opted out of those)

## Reference aspect

Aspect ratio 2:3 is invariant across all 9 source previews (333:500). Render at 1024×1536 to keep the slate-textured plastic detail crisp.

# Brand Identity Poster — Template

The 12 invariants restated with explicit pass/fail criteria for the validator.

## Format

- **Aspect ratio**: 4:5 vertical
- **Native resolution**: ≥1024×1280
- **Background**: dominantly logo-derived; near-black or near-white depending on logo tone
- **Layout**: multi-column grid, dense but balanced

## Section coverage (top to bottom, roughly)

1. **Header band** — brand name + 6-word statement + 3-word descriptors
2. **Color system** — 5-8 swatches with HEX + role labels + 1 gradient
3. **Typography tiers** — 3 type samples (headline / subhead / body) with real text
4. **Visual language tiles** — 3-5 image-style mood-board squares
5. **Brand applications** — 5+ mockups (packaging / web / mobile / social / card / billboard)
6. **Design system** — buttons + cards + inputs + nav + spacing scale
7. **Iconography** — 6-10 icons, consistent stroke weight, logo-derived geometry
8. **Pattern tile** — repeat pattern derived from logo
9. **Micro-detail tile** — shadow / foil / gloss / depth example

## Validator checklist

| # | Check | Pass criteria |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 4:5 aspect | output is portrait, ratio matches |
| 2 | Logo derivation | dominant colors visibly match the uploaded logo |
| 3 | ≥7 sections | count distinct labeled sections |
| 4 | Brand header complete | name + statement + 3 descriptors all visible |
| 5 | Color swatches | ≥5 swatches, each with HEX + role label |
| 6 | Typography tiers | 3 distinct type samples with real (legible) text |
| 7 | Visual language | 3-5 mood tiles present |
| 8 | Applications | ≥5 mockup categories visible |
| 9 | Design system | buttons + cards + at least one more component |
| 10 | Iconography | 6-10 icons, consistent style |
| 11 | Pattern tile | repeat pattern visible |
| 12 | Micro-detail tile | shadow / foil / gloss / depth example |

## Slot list

- `{BRAND_NAME}` — string, brand name in title case
- `{BRAND_STATEMENT}` — string, ≤6 words, declarative
- `{IDENTITY_DESCRIPTORS}` — array of 3 single-word adjectives, all-caps in output
- `{TONE}` — adjective, used to steer typography choice (`serif-led` for editorial, `sans-led` for tech, `mono-led` for raw)
- `{INDUSTRY}` — optional, used to pick mockup specifics (food packaging vs SaaS dashboard)
- Logo image — required, passed as reference

## Tone-to-typography mapping

| Tone | Headline | Subhead | Body |
|---|---|---|---|
| editorial / luxury | display serif (Tiempos / Editorial New) | sans-serif (Inter / Söhne) | serif body |
| tech / modern | display sans (Druk / Termina) | sans-serif (Inter / GT America) | sans body |
| raw / industrial | mono caps (Berkeley Mono / JetBrains) | sans-serif | mono body |
| playful | rounded sans (Söhne Breit / Recoleta) | rounded sans | rounded sans |

presets.template:
# Brand Logo Creative Director

> **Higgsfield image selector:** For Higgsfield still-image model choice, model shootouts, credit-sensitive image calls, or still keyframes before video, load `higgsfield-image-generation-playbook` first, then the narrow specialist.

Role: support skill, not a renderer. Use this before logo-oriented image-generation skills whenever taste, typography, brand continuity, reference-image interpretation, or production usability matters.

The core failure this skill prevents: treating a logo request as a pretty picture prompt. Logos are geometry, memory, constraints, and reproduction behavior. Image generation can help ideate; it cannot be trusted as the final judge of wordmark legibility or negative-space precision.

## When to run this first

Run this preflight before downstream logo/image skills when any of these are true:

- The user supplies a reference image, existing logo, sketch, mascot, or brand mark.
- The user asks for "thought out" variants, a concept sheet, directions, or territories.
- The output is meant to be brand-usable, not just inspirational art.
- The request involves wordmarks, monograms, letterforms, exact text, negative space, hidden objects, counters, cutouts, or geometric symbolism.
- The active style skill has rigid visual invariants that may conflict with the user's source brand.
- A previous generation failed OCR/readability, aspect ratio, geometry, or taste gates.

If the request is a purely decorative image in a logo-like style and the user does not need readable text or brand use, you may skip this and use the style skill directly.

## Classify the job

Before prompting any image backend, classify the request into one primary lane:

| Lane | Use when | Output posture |
|---|---|---|
| `ideation` | exploratory logo vibes, rough directions | image-gen-cli acceptable; label as inspiration |
| `reference reinterpretation` | user supplies a source mark/sketch | preserve source geometry first, style second |
| `negative-space` | hidden object, counters, letter cutouts | precision/vector lane unless explicitly exploratory |
| `wordmark/monogram` | exact letters or brand name are the mark | OCR gate required; deterministic typography preferred |
| `mascot/emblem` | animal/person/object mark with optional text | imagegen can draft mascot; compose text separately if final |
| `concept sheet` | 3+ variants with rationale | first define territories, then render/compose |
| `production/vector candidate` | user expects usable logo asset | SVG/text-mask/vector pipeline required |

State the lane briefly before generation. If a downstream style skill conflicts with the lane, the lane wins.

## Reference-image intake

When a source image exists, extract the brand DNA before choosing a style:

- **Word/letters:** exact visible text, casing, punctuation, spacing.
- **Silhouette:** blocky, rounded, condensed, wide, stacked, badge, icon-above-word, etc.
- **Weight:** stroke mass, black/white balance, counter size.
- **Geometry:** dominant angles, arcs, triangles, cuts, symmetry, baseline, x-height/cap-height relationships.
- **Personality:** industrial, academic, civic, playful, luxury, tech, retro, brutalist, organic, etc.
- **Non-negotiables:** what must survive in every variant.
- **Forbidden mutations:** what would make the mark stop feeling like the source.

Do not force a style-template invariant such as lowercase, rounded sans, gradient, mascot posture, or badge frame when it contradicts the source mark. Explain the conflict and adapt the style, or route to a different skill.

## Concept territories

For thoughtful variants, define 3-5 territories before rendering. Each territory needs:

- **Name:** 2-4 words.
- **Core metaphor:** one sentence.
- **Brand DNA preserved:** what source traits remain.
- **Visual mechanism:** how the mark works, especially where negative space or counters happen.
- **Risk:** what could fail in generation or production.
- **Best-use case:** where this direction fits.

Kill territories that differ only by decoration. A real logo territory changes the mechanism, not just the ornament.

## Backend routing

Use these routes deliberately:

| Need | Preferred route | Why |
|---|---|---|
| fast visual exploration | `image-gen-cli` + target style skill | good for taste and surprise |
| exact wordmark | deterministic type/SVG/PIL composition, then optional imagegen texture | text must not be hallucinated |
| negative-space mark | SVG/text-mask construction, or generated ideation followed by vector rebuild | cutouts need exact geometry |
| reference-mark preservation | pass reference image to `image-gen-cli` only for ideation; do not trust it as final | models drift from source geometry |
| raster-to-vector cleanup | `image-to-svg` test mode first; production only with user approval | vector credits cost money |
| hand-authored/vector logo | `svg-creator` with render-view-fix loop | production candidate requires visual verification |

Do not silently switch to credit-backed or paid backends. OAuth-backed `image-gen-cli` is pre-approved; Vectorizer.AI production mode and Higgsfield remain opt-in unless separately approved.

## Hard gates before handoff

A logo output cannot be called ready unless the relevant gates pass:

1. **Format/dimensions:** `file` or `sips` confirms requested format and aspect.
2. **Text gate:** OCR and/or visual inspection confirms exact requested text/casing. If OCR misreads a stylized mark, state that and require human visual confirmation before production claims.
3. **Negative-space gate:** hidden object/cutout is visible at normal size and does not destroy the letterform.
4. **Small-size gate:** preview at 64-128 px remains recognizable for icons/marks.
5. **No marketplace artifacts:** no watermark, seller signature, QR code, fake UI text, price tag, or random microcopy.
6. **Brand DNA gate:** source-mark non-negotiables survived.
7. **Production honesty:** generated raster outputs are labeled as concepts unless rebuilt/vectorized/approved as final art.

If a gate fails, do not polish around it. Either run one targeted retry, route to vector reconstruction, or stop and report the failed dimension.

## Downstream skill handoff

When handing off to a style skill, include a short directive block:

```text
BRAND LOGO CREATIVE DIRECTION
Lane: <lane>
Exact text/casing: <text>
Source DNA to preserve: <bullets>
Territory: <name + metaphor>
Allowed style adaptation: <what can change>
Forbidden mutations: <what must not change>
Validation gates: exact text, aspect, small-size, negative-space/geometry, no artifacts
Production status: ideation only | production/vector candidate
```

For negative-space skills, add:

```text
Negative-space priority: preserve letter readability first, hidden object second. Cutouts must replace counters/stems or connect cleanly to letter geometry. No leaky cutouts, chewed edges, decorative holes, or isolated icons that do not alter the mark.
```

## Failure handling

- If imagegen returns beautiful but unreadable text, reject it.
- If OCR fails on two attempts, route to deterministic typography/vector composition.
- If the generator ignores square/portrait constraints, crop/resize only when that does not alter the concept; then re-verify the final artifact.
- If the style skill's invariant causes brand mismatch, stop using that invariant for this task and explain why.
- If the user asks for final files, treat PNG as a proof, not the deliverable; create or request SVG/vector production steps.

## Output formats

### Quick preflight response

```text
Lane: <lane>
Brand DNA: <3-5 bullets>
Territories: <3 named options>
Recommended route: <backend/skill + why>
Validation gates: <checks>
```

### Concept sheet brief

```text
Brief: <one paragraph>
Source DNA: <bullets>
Territories:
1. <name> — <mechanism, risk, best use>
2. <name> — <mechanism, risk, best use>
3. <name> — <mechanism, risk, best use>
Production route: <ideation/vector/composite>
Rejection criteria: <hard stops>
```

## Related skills

- `creative-negative-space-logos` — use after this skill for Promptbase-style negative-space ideation.
- `highconverting-startup-logo-generator`, `modern-saas-vector-logo-generator`, `smart-minimal-logo-generator` — use after preflight for startup/SaaS marks.
- `minimal-mascot-logo-design`, `modern-iconic-mascot-logo-designs`, `pop-culture-emblem-logo-designs` — use after preflight for mascot/emblem lanes.
- `ultraminimalist-geometric-logos`, `minimal-typographic-logo-icon-style`, `minimalist-geometric-combination-logos`, `minimalist-screen-logo-generator`, `ultraminimalist-swiss-style-logos`, `minimal-monogram-logo-icon` — use after preflight for geometric/typographic lanes.
- `svg-creator` — use when final logo geometry must be deterministic.
- `image-to-svg` — use for raster-to-vector conversion; test mode first.
- `image-generation-skill-refiner` — use when modifying logo/imagegen skills to point at this preflight.

## Global Error Logging

When this skill is active and a skill-specific step fails while the working directory or any touched artifact is under `<vault>/wiki`, log the failure before retrying, skipping, or stopping.

Use the shared logger:

```bash
python3 ~/.agents/skills/bin/log-skill-error.py \
  --skill "brand-logo-creative-director" \
  --severity "ERROR" \
  --phase "<ingestion|analysis|generation|validation|write|tool>" \
  --tool "<tool or command>" \
  --message "<verbatim non-secret error or concise failure>" \
  --cwd "$PWD" \
  --artifact "<path if any>"
```

Rules:
- Log every non-transient error that affects the outcome, including tool rejection, schema or validation failure, missing auth, missing file, timeout, generation failure, malformed output, or blocked write.
- Preserve the original error string when safe. Do not log credentials, tokens, cookies, bearer headers, or other secrets.
- The logger always appends to `~/.craft-agent/logs/skill-errors.jsonl`. When the current directory or an artifact/source is under the wiki, it also mirrors the record to `<vault>/wiki/_logs/skill-errors.jsonl`.
- Continue normal failure handling after logging. Logging is evidence for repair, not a recovery substitute.

# BRANDKIT IMAGE GENERATION SKILL

## Christian global integration

- Installed globally from [https://github.com/Leonxlnx/taste-skill](https://github.com/Leonxlnx/taste-skill) at commit `339afcbf575daeaa61ee89646b3ba8912b308c39`.
- For HTML/widget deliverables, pick the structure first through `claude-design-widgets` → `html-wiki` → `html-widget-templates`; use this skill only for the aesthetic, art-direction, generation, or implementation layer described in its trigger.
- Do not override Christian-local rules for source-backed specifics, widget-template receipts, Craft preview sandboxing, image-generation metadata galleries, or fresh verification before completion.

You are an elite brand identity art director, logo designer, visual-system strategist, and presentation designer.

Your job is to generate premium brand-kit images that feel like they came from a serious identity studio.

The output must feel:
- intentional
- premium
- minimal
- coherent
- strategic
- visually expensive
- brand-system driven
- presentation-ready

Do not generate generic logos.  
Do not generate random mockups.  
Do not generate messy AI moodboards.

Create a complete brand world in one image.

---

# REFERENCE STYLE DNA

The desired visual quality is inspired by premium brand-guidelines decks with:

- dark charcoal outer canvas
- clean grid-based presentation boards
- strong gutters between panels
- restrained visual density
- very sparse typography
- large negative space
- cinematic brand atmosphere
- simple but memorable logo marks
- UI mockups used as brand applications
- browser chrome / app headers / terminal frames
- image-led panels with subtle overlays
- halftone, grain, scanline, or print texture
- geometric construction diagrams
- small labels and page-number details
- muted but powerful accent colors
- logo repeated across multiple touchpoints
- one strong brand idea per board

The references are not a fixed style.  
They define the quality bar, restraint, and presentation logic.

---

# CORE PRINCIPLE

A premium brand kit is not decoration.

It is a visual argument for why the brand exists.

Every generated board must answer:

1. What does this brand represent?
2. What is the core metaphor?
3. How does the logo express that?
4. How does the system scale across UI, print, image, and detail?
5. Why does the whole thing feel ownable?

---

# DEFAULT OUTPUT

Unless the user specifies otherwise:

- Generate one brand-kit overview image
- Default layout: `3 × 3`
- Default aspect ratio: `4:3` or `16:10`
- Use a clean presentation grid
- Use consistent gutters
- Use minimal text
- Make every panel feel connected

Allowed layouts:
- `3 × 3` full identity system
- `2 × 3` cinematic brand deck overview
- `2 × 2` compact concept board
- `1 × 3` horizontal brand strip
- `4 × 2` wide contact-sheet layout
- custom layout when requested

If the user gives references, match their quality and rhythm, not their exact content.

---

# BRAND STRATEGY FIRST

Before generating, infer the brand strategy.

Think through:

- category
- audience
- product function
- emotional promise
- cultural position
- trust level
- visual world
- symbolic metaphor
- what the brand should avoid

The visual system must be based on meaning.

Examples:

| Category | Core Ideas | Possible Symbol Logic |
|---|---|---|
| Developer tool | building, speed, precision, control | cursor, frame, bolt, scaffold, grid |
| AI assistant | delegation, intelligence, clarity | spark, orbit, signal, path, node |
| Security | protection, vigilance, boundary | shield, eye, seal, protected core |
| Gaming / betting | chance, reward, tension, speed | dice, gem, card, signal, trophy |
| Voice AI | sound, rhythm, command, flow | waveform, mic, orb, speech path |
| Compliance | trust, order, rules, protection | seal, dog, badge, document, shield |
| Drone / robotics | flight, control, vision, mission | wing, owl, crosshair, path, zone |
| Luxury / editorial | taste, material, ritual, restraint | monogram, seal, paper, emboss, mark |
| Productivity | focus, momentum, clarity | path, check, block, calendar, light |

Do not pick symbols randomly.

---

# LOGO GENERATION STANDARD

The logo must be professional.

It should be:
- simple
- memorable
- symbolic
- scalable
- ownable
- visually balanced
- connected to the brand idea
- usable as icon, wordmark, badge, UI mark, and pattern

Avoid:
- generic lightning bolts unless strongly justified
- random animals
- fake luxury crests
- copied famous marks
- overcomplicated symbols
- clipart-style icons
- meaningless sparkles
- inconsistent logo variants

The logo should feel like it came from research and reduction.

---

# LOGO CONCEPT METHODS

Use one or combine two maximum.

## 1. Monogram + Meaning

Combine the brand initial with a metaphor.

Examples:
- `K` + kite / frame / direction
- `N` + path / folded system
- `S` + sound wave / speech flow
- `A` + ascent / architecture / momentum

Do not make a boring letter icon.  
Use negative space, cuts, folds, or geometry.

---

## 2. Product Action

Turn the product's main action into a symbol.

Examples:
- build → frame, scaffold, block, cursor
- protect → shield, boundary, watch mark
- convert → switch, arrow, transformation shape
- speak → waveform, mic, pulse
- hunt threats → eye, raptor, radar, trace
- automate → loop, handoff, path

Make it abstract and premium, not literal.

---

## 3. Metaphor Fusion

Combine two meaningful ideas into one reduced mark.

Examples:
- owl + drone vision
- shield + mountain
- moon + waveform
- dog + compliance seal
- dice + mobile game economy
- cursor + lightning speed
- kite + product frame

The fusion should be subtle and readable.

---

## 4. Negative Space

Use empty space to create intelligence.

Examples:
- hidden arrow
- protected center
- cutout initial
- internal path
- folded corner
- eye formed by crossing shapes

Negative space should be crisp.

---

## 5. Construction Geometry

Create a mark from a clear system.

Use:
- circles
- diagonal cuts
- grids
- frames
- modular blocks
- layered cards
- orbital paths
- crosshairs
- measured linework

One panel can show construction logic.

---

# BOARD COMPOSITION DNA

A strong brand-kit board should feel like a curated sequence.

Use:
- large calm cover panel
- one digital mockup panel
- one image-led atmosphere panel
- one system/construction panel
- one physical or icon application panel
- one quiet tagline panel

Do not make every panel equally loud.

The board should have rhythm:
- quiet
- functional
- emotional
- technical
- atmospheric
- detailed

---

# DEFAULT 3 × 3 PANEL SYSTEM

Use this if no layout is specified:

## 1. Logo Cover
Large logo and wordmark.  
Minimal title.  
Strong negative space.

## 2. Logo Construction
Symbol breakdown, grid, geometry, or negative-space logic.  
Show why the mark exists.

## 3. Digital Application
Browser chrome, app header, terminal, dashboard fragment, or app icon.

## 4. Brand Essence
One short tagline.  
Large readable typography.  
Sparse composition.

## 5. Color System
Swatches, gradient strips, color discs, material chips, or palette cards.

## 6. Typography
Large type specimen, alphabet row, or primary/secondary type pairing.

## 7. Physical Application
Card, folder, badge, poster, label, seal, packaging, or object mockup.

## 8. Image Direction
Cinematic landscape, product crop, halftone poster, editorial scene, material texture.

## 9. System Detail
UI chips, input bar, command line, icon row, badge system, component strip, pattern detail.

---

# 2 × 3 REFERENCE-STYLE LAYOUT

For boards like the uploaded references, use:

1. **Logo / Wordmark**
   - centered or offset
   - extremely minimal

2. **Browser / Product Surface**
   - browser bar, app frame, prompt input, or URL field

3. **Command / Functional Panel**
   - terminal, prompt bar, input state, install command, dashboard fragment

4. **Atmosphere / Campaign Image**
   - halftone landscape, cinematic image, product-world visual, or art-directed photo

5. **Symbol / Construction / Badge**
   - logo mark in target, seal, geometric frame, icon construction

6. **Tagline / System Promise**
   - one short line
   - large type
   - quiet background

This layout should feel like a premium mini-deck.

---

# VISUAL MODES

Choose based on the brand.

## Dark Developer / Builder

Use for:
developer tools, coding agents, infra, automation, AI builders.

Visual cues:
- near-black panels
- monospace accents
- command lines
- terminal windows
- prompt bars
- subtle grid
- cyan, blue, coral, or lime accents
- pixel or CRT texture if appropriate

Logo logic:
- cursor + frame
- bolt + build speed
- scaffold + monogram
- terminal glyph + symbol
- modular construction mark

Mood:
precise, sharp, confident, builder-native.

---

## Dark Product / Operator

Use for:
business tools, growth tools, sales agents, automation, productivity.

Visual cues:
- black / dark red / amber
- glowing UI chips
- card systems
- segmented flows
- icon rows
- reward/progress motifs
- minimal hero text

Logo logic:
- signal, gift, path, operator mark, switch, loop, command system

Mood:
fast, operational, tactical, premium.

---

## Dark Nature / Calm System

Use for:
strategy, travel, wellness, climate, quiet premium SaaS.

Visual cues:
- deep green
- lime accent
- misty landscapes
- image UI circles
- soft overlays
- calm page labels
- dark editorial grid

Logo logic:
- path, leaf, moon, horizon, compass, portal, folded mark

Mood:
calm, trustworthy, focused.

---

## Dark Security / Threat Intelligence

Use for:
security, compliance, monitoring, network products.

Visual cues:
- black/navy
- shield forms
- radar lines
- threat labels
- subtle motion traces
- red/blue alert chips
- controlled gradients

Logo logic:
- shield, raptor, eye, watch, boundary, protected core

Mood:
serious, vigilant, precise.

---

## Light Editorial / Compliance

Use for:
legal, privacy, compliance, documents, trust brands.

Visual cues:
- warm ivory
- paper texture
- small serif labels
- seals / badges
- color wheel / palette object
- calm stationery
- deep blue, red, gold accents

Logo logic:
- seal, dog, shield, document, stamp, monogram

Mood:
trustworthy, refined, institutional but modern.

---

## Luxury / Beauty / Fashion

Use for:
beauty, fashion, hospitality, premium services.

Visual cues:
- ivory / stone / espresso
- serif wordmark
- elegant monogram
- paper grain
- embossing
- product labels
- editorial crops
- soft shadows

Logo logic:
- monogram, seal, petal, vessel, ritual object, refined typographic mark

Mood:
tasteful, adult, expensive.

---

## Voice / Communication

Use for:
voice AI, chat, assistants, speech, audio.

Visual cues:
- dark indigo
- lilac glow
- waveform
- mic motif
- phone crop
- command input
- app icon

Logo logic:
- wave + initial
- sound orb
- speech path
- microphone abstraction
- pulse ring

Mood:
fluid, intelligent, intimate.

---

## Cultural / Experimental

Use for:
music, creative tools, events, gaming-adjacent, cultural products.

Visual cues:
- halftone
- CRT texture
- analog print
- bold accent color
- poster-style panels
- unexpected image crops
- simple but punchy logo

Logo logic:
- custom wordmark
- icon with attitude
- symbolic mascot
- print-inspired mark

Mood:
memorable, creative, still controlled.

---

# PREMIUM DETAIL LANGUAGE

Use details like:
- small page numbers
- tiny footer labels
- precise alignment marks
- construction lines
- subtle crosshair grids
- thin rules
- browser bars
- rounded rectangles
- image masks
- soft shadows
- low-opacity texture
- halftone image treatment
- one highlighted word
- one accent chip
- one strong icon state

Do not overuse them.

Premium detail should reward looking closer.

---

# TEXT RULES

Use very little text.

Good text:
- brand name
- one tagline
- one URL
- one command
- 2–5 section labels
- short UI chips

Bad text:
- long paragraphs
- tiny fake body copy
- lots of menu items
- lorem ipsum
- dense explan

# 3D Glossy Candy Icons Template

Source listing: [Promptbase — 3D Glossy Candy Like Icons by @astsal1](https://promptbase.com/prompt/3d-glossy-candy-like-icons-2). Reverse-engineered from 9 public preview images. Engine target: `gpt_image_2` at `quality=high`, aspect `1:1`.

## Required invariants (verbatim — reproduce in every prompt)

1. 1:1 square aspect ratio. Output size 1024x1024.
2. Exactly one hero subject ({OBJECT}), centered horizontally and vertically, occupying 60–70 percent of the frame height.
3. Material is glossy candy-coated plastic: smooth seamless surfaces, softly rounded edges, inflated puffy proportions. No metal, no roughness, no scratches, no texture grain.
4. Monochromatic palette: the subject and the background sit in the same {COLOR} hue family. Background is a flat wall in {COLOR}, the subject is the same hue rendered in dimensional plastic. No gradients, no patterns.
5. Soft top-left ambient studio lighting. Gentle diffuse specular highlights along the subject's upper-left edges. No rim lights, no harsh contrast, no caustics.
6. Three-quarter view with a slight tilt for dimensionality. Subject floats slightly above an imagined ground plane.
7. Soft circular drop shadow directly beneath the subject. Single shadow, low opacity, blurred edges.
8. Clean negative space. No ground plane, no horizon line, no environment, no second object.
9. Absolutely no text, no labels, no callouts, no QR codes, no price tags, no watermarks, no seller signatures (no "astsal1" or any other handle).
10. Pixar-meets-Blender pastel candy aesthetic: smooth subsurface-feeling plastic, gentle reflections, no photographic realism, no painterly brushwork.

| Slot | Type | Default | Notes |

| {COLOR} | string, single hue word | — | required. Pastel-leaning hues land best (pink, lavender, mint, peach, sky blue, coral, butter yellow, lilac, blush). The same word fills both subject and background. |

Pixar-meets-Blender pastel candy aesthetic, smooth subsurface-feeling plastic, no metal, no roughness, no scratches. Square 1:1 aspect ratio, 1024x1024. # Template: Black White Cute Vector Icon Logos

Reverse-engineered from 9 preview images of the Promptbase listing **Black White Cute Vector Icon Logos** by @divdev. Synthesized via `codex-cli-subagent` (GPT-5.5) triangulation.

## Aspect ratio

`1:1` (square). Use `--size "square 1024x1024 PNG"` with `image-gen-cli`.

## Required invariants (the contract)

1. 1:1 square canvas
2. single centered icon mark
3. solid black background
4. pure white fill on the subject
5. high-contrast cute-spooky cartoon vector mascot
6. simple rounded clean linework
7. no text labels
8. mascot face filling most of the frame
9. thick chunky strokes/shapes
10. optional small props (hat, top-hat, glasses, scarf)
11. subtle internal black detailing inside the white shapes for facial features

## Variable slots

| Slot           | Type                                                          | Required | Default                     | Notes                                                                                            |
|----------------|---------------------------------------------------------------|----------|-----------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| ICON_SUBJECT   | string (free-form)                                            | yes      | (none)                      | The cute-spooky-cartoon mascot, e.g. "skull in a top hat", "ghost holding a balloon", "snowman with crossed bandages". |
| ACCESSORY      | string (free-form, optional)                                  | no       | `""` (none)                 | Optional small prop on or around the mascot.                                                     |
| MOOD           | enum: `cute-spooky` \| `cute-creepy` \| `cute-grim` \| `cute-festive` | no       | `cute-spooky`               | Adjusts the emotional register without breaking invariants.                                      |
| BACKGROUND     | string                                                         | no       | `solid pure black #000000` | Changing this inverts invariants 3 and 4. Confirm with the user before generating.               |

## Prompt skeleton

Verbatim from triangulation. Substitute every `{SLOT}`, then send to `image-gen-cli`.

```
Create a 1:1 square canvas with a {BACKGROUND}. Place a single centered icon mark of {ICON_SUBJECT}, with {ACCESSORY} if provided, in a {MOOD} mood. Render a high-contrast cute-spooky cartoon vector mascot with pure white fill on the subject, mascot face filling most of the frame, thick chunky strokes/shapes, simple rounded clean linework, and subtle internal black detailing inside the white shapes for facial features. Use thick chunky rounded vector shapes and a clean centered silhouette with no outlines. Keep it as a single centered white-fill mascot on a solid black background, with optional small props (hat, top-hat, glasses, scarf) only when they support the subject. No text labels, no text, no signature, no watermark, no shadow, no gradient. Avoid style deviation: modern cute-spooky vector mascot logo, sticker-ready, hi-contrast monochrome.
```

## Self-test demo subject

`cute-spooky ghost mascot wearing oversized round glasses`

Default self-test slot values (used to render `icon.png`):

```json
{
  "ICON_SUBJECT": "cute-spooky ghost mascot wearing oversized round glasses",
  "ACCESSORY": "oversized round glasses",
  "MOOD": "cute-spooky",
  "BACKGROUND": "solid pure black #000000"
}
```

## Failure modes observed in triangulation

These were single-preview decorations that DO NOT belong in the invariant block:

- small black detail variations
- specific facial-expression quirks
- promptbase watermarks (none observed in this corpus, but listed defensively)
- asymmetric accessory placements
- color shifts

If a generation introduces any of the above as a "feature" of the style, treat it as drift and re-run.

# Frosted Depth Icon Grids Template

## Required invariants (verbatim — reproduce in every prompt)

1. 2:3 source-aspect visual system; for skill UI icon.png, center the source-aspect board inside a square app-icon canvas.
2. vertical 2:3 canvas
3. centered 3 by 4 icon grid
4. generous even spacing
5. soft frosted translucent 3D icons
6. rounded beveled 3D forms
7. soft glossy specular highlights
8. soft studio lighting
9. subtle shadows under each icon
10. no main headline or body copy

## Variable slots

| Slot | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| {HERO_SUBJECT} | string, icon theme or category | twelve outdoor adventure and weather utility icons | required; Theme for the twelve icons; observed values included travel, wellness, communication, fashion, crypto, smart home, sustainability, gaming, and mixed app-style icons. |
| {BACKGROUND} | string, clean matte color or smooth gradient | deep teal-to-slate smooth gradient background | required; Background treatment behind the grid; keep it clean, minimal, flat, matte, or softly gradient. |
| {PALETTE} | string, translucent glass color palette | translucent aqua, coral, warm amber, soft lavender, and milky white glass | required; Controls the candy-glass icon colors and accents while preserving frosted translucent material. |
| {ICON_SET} | string, optional twelve-icon list in grid order | compass, folded trail map, mountain peak, pine tree, sun, puffy cloud, raindrop, lightning bolt, camp lantern, binoculars, backpack, location pin | optional; Use when exact icons matter; list left-to-right, top-to-bottom across the 3 by 4 grid. |

## Prompt skeleton

<!-- format: prose -->

```text
Negative directives: no swastika, no SS insignia, no fasces, no iron cross, no hammer-and-sickle, no historical fascist or communist iconography, no armband on any figure, no resemblance to any historical dictator or political leader, no Axis-power or Soviet uniform regalia.

Create a "vertical 2:3 canvas" showing a "centered 3 by 4 icon grid" of {HERO_SUBJECT} on {BACKGROUND}. Use exactly twelve icons; if provided, follow this left-to-right, top-to-bottom icon list: {ICON_SET}. Keep "generous even spacing", consistent scale, and isolated centered placement in each grid cell. Render every object as "soft frosted translucent 3D icons" with "rounded beveled 3D forms", candy-gel thickness, semi-transparent bodies, subtle internal refraction, "soft glossy specular highlights", inner glow, and delicate rim highlights. Use {PALETTE} for the translucent material colors and small accents. Apply "soft studio lighting" from the upper left, ambient occlusion, and "subtle shadows under each icon" falling gently down-right. Keep the composition polished, minimal, high-resolution, product-icon-like, with no border, no frame, no watermark, no seller signature, no QR code, no price tag, no marketplace overlay, and "no main headline or body copy". Avoid labels or captions; allow only tiny symbolic marks that are structurally necessary for a requested icon.
```

## Safety guardrail

The prompt skeleton includes this standing negative directive and it must remain in all generated variants: no swastika, no SS insignia, no fasces, no iron cross, no hammer-and-sickle, no historical fascist or communist iconography, no armband on any figure, no resemblance to any historical dictator or political leader, no Axis-power or Soviet uniform regalia.

presets.template:
# Fun Pop Art Postage Stamps Template

Source: Promptbase "Fun Pop Art Postage Stamps" by @promptfactor, ChatGPT-Image-2.

## Required invariants (verbatim — reproduce in every prompt)

1. 2:3 vertical aspect ratio. Output size 1024×1536.
2. Stamp shape: rectangular vertical postage stamp with a bold white scalloped perforated border
   running on all four sides, and a thin cream/off-white interior margin between the perforation
   and the artwork. The stamp sits on a small cream/parchment background.
3. Single iconic landmark hero. Frontal hero-shot framing. Hero occupies the lower 55–65% of the
   stamp interior, centered horizontally.
4. Bold black ink outlines on every shape. Comic-book / Roy Lichtenstein pop art line weight.
5. Flat saturated pop-art palette only: red, yellow, blue, green, black, white. No realistic
   shading. No photographic lighting. No gradients on the landmark itself, only halftone for
   value.
6. Roy Lichtenstein Ben Day halftone dots in the sky / background band. Dense, evenly spaced,
   white-on-color or color-on-color.
7. Top scroll-ribbon banner across the upper portion of the stamp interior, yellow background,
   with verbatim copy {LANDMARK} in chunky bold all-caps yellow letters with a red drop shadow.
   The ribbon has small black-outlined fold tabs at left and right ends.
8. Bottom scroll-ribbon banner across the lower portion of the stamp interior, either yellow or
   green background, with verbatim copy {COUNTRY} in the same chunky bold all-caps style.
9. Optional denomination tag in the upper-right corner: a yellow circle, yellow rectangle, or
   blue circle (small) containing the verbatim copy {DENOMINATION} (e.g. "20¢", "60", "33¢")
   in bold black or red. Omit the tag if {DENOMINATION} is empty.
10. No watermark. No seller signature. No QR code. No price tag. No extra text outside the two
    banners and the optional denomination tag.
11. Quote {LANDMARK}, {COUNTRY}, and {DENOMINATION} verbatim in the prompt — pop-art typography
    is unforgiving and any deviation will rerender as a different word.

## Variable slots

| Slot | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| {LANDMARK} | string, 1–4 words, all caps in render | — | required, e.g. "MOUNT FUJI", "STATUE OF LIBERTY" |
| {COUNTRY} | string, 1–3 words, all caps in render | — | required, e.g. "JAPAN", "UNITED KINGDOM" |
| {DENOMINATION} | string, 1–3 chars (digits + optional ¢) | "" | optional; when "" the tag is omitted |
| {LANDMARK_VISUAL} | string | "the iconic landmark itself, frontal hero shot" | what to actually draw |
| {SKY_HUE} | enum: red \| yellow \| orange \| yellow-to-red gradient | yellow-to-red gradient | always with halftone dots over it |
| {GROUND_HUE} | enum: red \| green \| yellow \| blue (water) | red rolling hills | landmark-appropriate |
| {DENOM_TAG} | enum: yellow-circle \| yellow-rectangle \| blue-circle | yellow-circle | only used when {DENOMINATION} is non-empty |
| {ACCENTS} | string, optional | "two small white rounded clouds upper-left" | small decorations only — clouds, sun, water lines |

## Prompt skeleton

```
A pop art comic-book style postage stamp, vertical 2:3 aspect, with a bold white scalloped
perforated border on all four sides framing a small cream/parchment interior margin. Inside the
stamp, a hero shot of {LANDMARK_VISUAL} occupying the lower 55–65% of the frame, centered
horizontally, drawn with bold black ink outlines on every shape and flat saturated pop-art comic
colors only — red, yellow, blue, green, black, white — no realistic shading, no photographic
light, no gradients on the landmark itself. The sky is a {SKY_HUE} band covered in dense,
evenly spaced Roy Lichtenstein Ben Day halftone dots. {ACCENTS}. Below the landmark, a
{GROUND_HUE} foreground. A top scroll-ribbon banner across the upper portion of the stamp reads
"{LANDMARK}" in chunky bold all-caps yellow letters with a red drop shadow, on a yellow ribbon
with small black-outlined fold tabs at the ends. A bottom scroll-ribbon banner across the lower
portion reads "{COUNTRY}" in the same chunky bold all-caps style. {DENOM_BLOCK}. No watermark,
no signature, no QR code, no extra text outside these banners and the denomination tag. Output
1024×1536.
```

Where `{DENOM_BLOCK}` resolves to one of:
- `(when DENOMINATION non-empty)`: `A small {DENOM_TAG} in the upper-right corner contains "{DENOMINATION}" in bold black, with a black outline.`
- `(when DENOMINATION empty)`: `No denomination tag.`

## Negative reinforcement (append when iterating after a failed self-test)

- "No realistic photo, no 3D rendering, no soft shading, no airbrush, no gradient on the
  landmark."
- "Halftone dots are uniform and dense — not sparse, not painterly."
- "Banner type is chunky 3D-feeling sans-serif, not thin, not script."
- "Only one stamp in the frame. Do not tile or grid multiple stamps."

## Canonical demo subject (used to render `icon.png`)

- {LANDMARK} = "GATEWAY ARCH"
- {COUNTRY} = "ST LOUIS"
- {DENOMINATION} = "26¢"
- {LANDMARK_VISUAL} = "the Gateway Arch, full silvery silhouette catenary curve rising over a
  green riverfront"
- {SKY_HUE} = "yellow-to-red gradient"
- {GROUND_HUE} = "blue river ground stripe"
- {DENOM_TAG} = "yellow-circle"
- {ACCENTS} = "one small white rounded cloud upper-left, halftone sun upper-right"

This subject exercises every invariant: arch silhouette tests bold-line discipline, river tests
ground-hue slot, "GATEWAY ARCH" tests two-word top banner, "ST LOUIS" tests two-word bottom
banner, "26¢" tests denomination tag with cents glyph.

# Hyperclean Minimalist 3D Icons Template

<!-- format: json-spec -->

## Required invariants (verbatim — reproduce in every prompt)

1. 1:1 square canvas. Output size 1024×1024 PNG.
2. centered single hero object.
3. hyperclean minimalist 3D icon style.
4. rounded inflated geometry.
5. satin-gloss material finish.
6. soft upper-left studio lighting.
7. subtle ambient occlusion.
8. large negative space.
9. warm off-white seamless background.
10. diffuse oval ground shadow.
11. no outline strokes.
12. no text/typography.
13. no watermark, no SamMelk text, no QR codes, no price tag, no seller signature.

## Variable slots

| Slot | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| {HERO_SUBJECT} | string or image ref | — | required. The single centered inflated 3D object, creature, food, character, hand gesture, or symbol. |
| {PALETTE} | string, 2-3 dominant colors | warm pastel hero colors | Dominant hero colors and small accent colors; keep warm, soft, and high-key unless the user overrides. |
| {BACKGROUND} | string | warm off-white/cream seamless studio background | Background surface color only; preserve the clean studio backdrop, large negative space, and no texture/no scene rule. |
| {POSE} | string | front-facing or slight three-quarter product-icon pose | Hero orientation, gesture, tilt, or floating stance, such as diagonal upward rocket, peace-sign hand, waving mascot, or heart-hands. |
| {ACCENT_PROPS} | string | none | Optional attached details or props such as steam wisps, torus ring, toppings, flame plume, sunglasses, porthole, or other subject-specific accents. |
| {FACIAL_FEATURES} | string | none unless the subject is a mascot or character | Simple kawaii face details when applicable; usually glossy black oval eyes and a small smile, integrated into the inflated form. |

# Minimalist Screen Logo Generator Template

## Required invariants (verbatim — reproduce in every prompt)

1. 1:1 square logo tile. Output size 1024×1024 PNG.
2. 1:1 square canvas
3. plain white background
4. centered display icon
5. flat vector logo style
6. dark bezel
7. simple dark stand and base
8. vivid gradient screen fill
9. large bold white uppercase headline
10. bold uppercase sans-serif text
11. ample white negative space
12. No watermark, no seller signature, no QR codes, no price tags.
13. Text accuracy — quote every screen-label or logo-copy slot verbatim in the prompt.
14. Safety exclusions — no swastika, no SS insignia, no fasces, no iron cross, no hammer-and-sickle, no historical fascist or communist iconography, no armband on any figure, no resemblance to any historical dictator or political leader, no Axis-power or Soviet uniform regalia.

presets.template:
# Template: Modern 3D Icon Collection Sets

Source listing: <https://promptbase.com/prompt/modern-3d-icon-collection-sets>
Aspect ratio: **2:3 portrait** (use `--size "portrait 1024x1536 PNG"` with image-gen-cli)
Prompt format: **json-spec**

## Invariants (every generation must satisfy all)

1. vertical 2:3 composition
2. centered icons with even spacing
3. rounded beveled 3D forms
4. single-material monochrome look
5. ambient occlusion contact shadows
6. minimal seamless background
7. no labels or captions

Decorations the source carries on individual previews but the template drops:
- single-preview embedded currency glyphs
- single-preview raised Z glyph

## Variable slots

- `{HERO_THEME}` (string, required=True) - The themed icon collection subject; observed values vary across fintech, education, travel, social, web, kitchen, eco, restaurant, and wellness sets.
- `{ICON_COUNT_AND_GRID}` (string, required=True) - Count plus grid geometry, e.g. "3x4 grid of 12 icons" or "4x5 grid of 20 icons"; preserve centered catalogue spacing.
- `{PALETTE_BAND}` (string, required=True) - Single-hue or mood-gradient color band applied coherently to icons, shadows, glow, and background.
- `{ICON_LIST}` (ordered list, required=True) - Specific icons to render, preferably row-by-row in grid order.
- `{BACKGROUND_DETAIL}` (string, required=True) - Matte seamless or mood-band background treatment, including vignette, gradient, haze, or tonal depth.
- `{LIGHTING_DIRECTION}` (string, required=True) - Soft studio light direction; previews are mostly upper-left with one upper-right variant.
- `{DEPTH_AND_BLUR_RULE}` (string, required=True) - Shadow offset, ambient occlusion strength, blur softness, and depth separation rules.

## Prompt skeleton

The literal block below is the engine input. Substitute every `{SLOT}` with the slot value supplied by the caller, then pass the result as `--prompt` to image-gen-cli's wrapper. Do not paraphrase the invariants list; gpt-image-2 keys off the exact wording.

```
JSON spec:
{
  "model_target": "gpt-image-2",
  "output": {
    "aspect_ratio": "2:3 portrait",
    "size": "1024x1536"
  },
  "brief": "Create {HERO_THEME}.",
  "required_invariants": [
    "vertical 2:3 composition",
    "centered icons with even spacing",
    "rounded beveled 3D forms",
    "single-material monochrome look",
    "ambient occlusion contact shadows",
    "minimal seamless background",
    "no labels or captions"
  ],
  "layout": {
    "grid": "{ICON_COUNT_AND_GRID}",
    "composition": "centered catalogue grid with generous even spacing, consistent icon scale, balanced portrait margins",
    "icon_order": "{ICON_LIST}",
    "camera": "orthographic to front three-quarter, minimal perspective, each icon isolated and fully visible"
  },
  "surface_fidelity": {
    "icon_material": "frosted-glass / soft clay-plastic depth icons with rounded inflated volumes, beveled edges, smooth matte translucency, subtle specular highlights, and coherent single-material rendering",
    "palette_band": "{PALETTE_BAND}",
    "background": "smooth mood-band background: {BACKGROUND_DETAIL}",
```

# Modern Flat Icon Stickers Template

> Fidelity is locked. Enhancement is a separate, explicit request after acceptance.

## Unanimous structural invariants

1. One isolated, highly simplified icon-like subject is centered in a square frame with broad open pink negative space. (9/9 previews)
2. The subject uses a white interior with dominant heavy black rounded contour work and sparse color only for a small expressive accent. (9/9 previews)
3. A thick, irregular white die-cut sticker border and a restrained dark gray shadow offset down-left frame every icon. (9/9 previews)

## Discriminative signatures

### A faint, clean interlocking jigsaw-piece seam pattern visibly crosses both the sticker and its backing field.
- Evidence: preview-01.png, preview-02.png, preview-03.png, preview-04.png, preview-05.png, preview-06.png, preview-07.png, preview-08.png, preview-09.png (9/9 previews)
- Discriminative weight: 5/5
- Prompt clause: a faint clean interlocking jigsaw-piece seam pattern crossing both sticker and pink backing field, only within the flat canvas plane
- Medium/process/substrate: flat digital sticker illustration · bold rounded ink-like vector contours with a die-cut presentation · matte flat pink backing with a subtle puzzle-seam overlay
- Irregularity: not marked purposeful
- Composition exception: The seam overlay may traverse the subject but must stay faint enough not to compromise the silhouette.

### The black contour weight is oversized, round-capped, and playful, with simplified facial and object details rather than refined vector geometry.
- Evidence: preview-01.png, preview-02.png, preview-03.png, preview-04.png, preview-05.png, preview-06.png, preview-07.png, preview-08.png, preview-09.png (9/9 previews)
- Discriminative weight: 5/5
- Prompt clause: oversized round-capped playful black contours with deliberately simplified facial or object details
- Medium/process/substrate: flat black-and-white cartoon line art · high-contrast monoline drawing with rounded caps and sparse fill · clean white sticker face
- Irregularity: purposeful
- Composition exception: Contour bends and tiny facial marks may be playfully asymmetric but the outer silhouette remains clean.

### Small pink, orange, or lime accent marks punctuate an otherwise white-and-black icon without becoming a multicolor illustration.
- Evidence: preview-01.png, preview-03.png, preview-04.png, preview-05.png, preview-06.png, preview-07.png, preview-09.png (7/9 previews)
- Discriminative weight: 4/5
- Prompt clause: do not turn the icon into a multicolor illustration
- Medium/process/substrate: limited-color sticker print · one accent ink placed as small punctuation against black and white · matte pink backing
- Irregularity: not marked purposeful
- Composition exception: A subject with no natural accent may use a tiny badge, blush, flame, or motion mark instead.

## Variable slots

| Slot | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---:|---|---|
| `{SUBJECT}` | icon subject | yes | playful skull wearing sunglasses | A single bold icon subject; bind acceptance subjects here. |
| `{ACCENT_COLOR}` | color | yes | coral pink | Use one restrained accent color only. |

- **clean background without source texture** — likely failure: The rendered sticker loses the defining jigsaw overlay or makes it too strong to read as a sticker.; countermeasure: Require a faint clean interlocking puzzle seam that crosses sticker and backing yet never compromises the silhouette.

## Fidelity-locked prompt skeleton

Create a completely original modern flat icon sticker of one isolated centered {SUBJECT}, fully visible in a square frame with broad open pink negative space. The entire square canvas must be opaque, flat, uniform pale coral-pink from edge to edge, with no transparency, black field, vignette, texture, external puzzle pieces, splashes, or elements beyond the one sticker. Use a white interior, dominant heavy black rounded contour work, and only sparse {ACCENT_COLOR} expressive accents. Draw it with oversized round-capped playful black contours with deliberately simplified facial or object details. Add a thick irregular white die-cut sticker border and a restrained dark-gray shadow offset down-left. Overlay a faint clean interlocking jigsaw-piece seam pattern crossing both sticker and pink backing field, only within the flat canvas plane; keep it subtle and continuous, never as loose fragments. Keep color restrained to small {ACCENT_COLOR} punctuation marks; do not turn the icon into a multicolor illustration. Matte, flat, high-contrast, playful graphic-sticker presentation. No text, letters, numbers, logos, watermark, fake UI, photorealism, 3D rendering, gradients, extra objects, or cropped silhouette.

## Optional enhancement boundary

Do not improve, polish, modernize, or reinterpret this skeleton during cloning or ordinary use. After a fidelity-passing render exists, an explicit user request may authorize a separate enhancement variant; keep the accepted fidelity-locked skeleton unchanged.
