# Vintage Cartoon Mascot Logos Template

Reproduces the Promptbase listing "Vintage Cartoon Mascot Logos" by @promptlydesigned (Gemini 2.5-Flash-Image). Output backend is Higgsfield `gpt_image_2` at `quality=high`. Listing reverse-engineered from 9 public preview images + 1 cover collage on 2026-05-03.

## Required invariants (verbatim — reproduce in every prompt)

1. **1:1 square canvas. Output 1024×1024.** Plain off-white / cream solid background outside the badge. No scenery, no patterns, no drop shadows behind the badge.
2. **One centered circular badge** as the only graphic element. Diameter ~80–88% of canvas height, geometrically perfect circle.
3. **Top-arc business name** = `{ARC_TOP}` curved along the upper arc of the ring, bold sans-serif, default ALL CAPS (Title Case allowed when `{ARC_CASE}=title`). Letters follow the curve precisely with even spacing.
4. **Bottom-arc descriptor** = `{ARC_BOTTOM}` curved along the lower arc, same family, slightly smaller.
5. **Ring variant** = `{RING_VARIANT}`:
   - `outline` (default): single or double stroke ring in `{ACCENT_COLOR}` or black, interior is `{INTERIOR_FILL}` (white | cream | accent-tint).
   - `filled-band`: thick solid `{ACCENT_COLOR}` band carries arc type in reverse-out cream lettering. Interior is cream.
6. **Hero mascot** = `{HERO_MASCOT}`, a single anthropomorphic 1930s rubber-hose cartoon character occupying the center of the badge (3/4 to full body). Mandatory rubber-hose features: round head with big dot or oval eyes, cheerful open smile, white-gloved hands, noodle limbs, simple round-toe shoes when feet are visible.
7. **Action prop** = `{HERO_PROP}` held in at least one gloved hand, semantically tied to the business implied by `{ARC_BOTTOM}`.
8. **Strict two-color palette**: solid black ink + exactly one saturated `{ACCENT_COLOR}`. No gradients. No halftone. No photographic or 3D shading. Flat fills only. Monochrome variant allowed (accent-on-cream with no separate black ink, type and outline both rendered in `{ACCENT_COLOR}`).
9. **Vector aesthetic**: clean even-weight ink outlines, solid color fills, geometric construction. Looks designed in Illustrator, not painted.
10. **Optional ornaments** = `{ORNAMENT_DOTS}`: small dot or diamond separators at the 9 and 3 o'clock positions between arc text, OR small swirl curls inside the ring near the mascot's feet. Use sparingly — at most one ornament type per logo.
11. **No watermark, no seller signature, no QR codes, no price tags, no slogans, no taglines outside the two arcs, no URLs, no email addresses.**
12. **Text accuracy** — quote `{ARC_TOP}` and `{ARC_BOTTOM}` verbatim in the prompt. Spell-check before rendering.

## Variable slots

| Slot | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `{ARC_TOP}` | string, 1-4 words | — | required, business name |
| `{ARC_BOTTOM}` | string, 1-3 words | — | required, descriptor (e.g. "BAKERY", "ROASTERS", "Donut Shop") |
| `{HERO_MASCOT}` | string | — | required, e.g. "round-headed boy in chef's toque", "anthropomorphic donut", "long-eared rubber-hose dog" |
| `{HERO_PROP}` | string | — | required, e.g. "wooden rolling pin overhead", "steaming coffee mug", "blue dumbbell", "scissors" |
| `{ACCENT_COLOR}` | string | "saturated red" | required, single saturated color name; common choices: red, cyan, navy, plum, teal, brown, mustard yellow, mint green |
| `{INTERIOR_FILL}` | enum: white, cream, accent-tint | white | optional override |
| `{ARC_CASE}` | enum: uppercase, title | uppercase | optional |
| `{RING_VARIANT}` | enum: outline, filled-band | outline | optional |
| `{ORNAMENT_DOTS}` | enum: none, dots, swirls | none | optional flair |

## Prompt skeleton (engine input)

```
Vintage 1930s rubber-hose cartoon mascot logo. A perfectly circular badge centered on a clean off-white solid background, square 1:1 canvas. Ring variant: {RING_VARIANT}. The top arc reads "{ARC_TOP}" in bold sans-serif {ARC_CASE} type, the bottom arc reads "{ARC_BOTTOM}" in the same type family slightly smaller, both curving precisely along the ring. Inside the circle, a single anthropomorphic 1930s rubber-hose cartoon mascot: {HERO_MASCOT}. The mascot has the canonical rubber-hose look — round head, big dot or oval eyes, cheerful open smile, white-gloved hands, noodle limbs, simple round-toe shoes if feet are visible. The mascot is holding {HERO_PROP} in at least one gloved hand, in a pose that reads instantly as the business named in the bottom arc. Strict two-color palette: solid black ink plus saturated {ACCENT_COLOR}. Interior fill of the badge: {INTERIOR_FILL}. Flat vector aesthetic — single-weight clean ink outlines, solid color fills, no gradients, no halftone, no photographic shading, no 3D render. Geometric construction, looks designed in Adobe Illustrator. Optional ornament: {ORNAMENT_DOTS}. Absolutely no watermark, no seller signature, no QR code, no price tag, no slogan, no tagline outside the two arcs, no URLs, no extra text. Text accuracy: render "{ARC_TOP}" and "{ARC_BOTTOM}" exactly as written.
```

## Negative prompt (append for stubborn drift)

> Not photoreal. No 3D. No gradient shading. No watercolor. No halftone unless explicitly invoked. No modern flat-illustration big-head trend. No drop shadow behind the badge. No multiple mascots. No text outside the two arcs. No watermark "promptlydesigned" or any seller signature. No multi-color rainbow palette — only one saturated accent.

<!-- format: layout-as-prompt -->
<!-- COLOR-FIRST STRUCTURE. ## Required invariants (verbatim — reproduce in every prompt)

1. Vertical iPhone-wallpaper aspect, rendered at 1024×1536 PNG (portrait 2:3, reading as 9:16 phone lock-screen proportions).
2. Exactly one hero animal of species/breed `{PET_BREED}`, full-body or near-full-body, moving forward toward the camera in a species-appropriate gait. Anatomy must be natural and believable.
3. Behind the animal sits a **giant Instagram-style polaroid post frame**: white or off-white border with rounded corners, small circular profile avatar at the top, the handle `{USERNAME}` rendered in clean small sans-serif beside the avatar, and a thin row of social-style icons (heart / comment / share / bookmark abstractions) below the image area. Recognizable as a social-media post layout, **not** an exact replica of any real platform UI. No platform logos, no verified badge.
4. **Frame-break composition**: the animal's body physically extends past the frame edges. The closest body part to the camera (`{FOREGROUND_BODY_PART}`) is the foreground anchor and breaks past the bottom or front edge of the frame, enlarged by dramatic wide-angle lens distortion.
5. **Dramatic low-angle wide-angle perspective** with strong depth and perspective distortion. Camera near ground level; lens behaves like a 14-24mm wide. Only the single foreground limb is enlarged; the rest of the body remains anatomically correct.
6. **Background**: `{BACKGROUND_THEME}` with bright blue sky, soft white cumulus clouds, warm golden sunlight shining through, flowers and plants flanking the frame, and 1-3 butterflies in the air. Atmosphere reads `{MOOD}`, cute, healing, whimsical, fairy-tale.

Premium commercial pet-photography quality.

9. **No watermark, no seller signature, no QR codes, no platform logo, no price tag, no extra captions.** Only the `{USERNAME}` text appears.

```
Create an iPhone-sized vertical wallpaper of a {PET_BREED} naturally emerging from a giant Instagram-style polaroid post frame.

The polaroid frame is a clean white card with rounded corners. At the top of the frame there is a small circular profile avatar and the handle "{USERNAME}" rendered in clean small sans-serif. Below the image area there is a thin row of social-style icons (heart, comment, share, bookmark) drawn as simple line glyphs. The frame is clearly recognizable as a social-media post layout but does NOT copy any real platform UI exactly. No platform logo, no verified-badge tick.

The animal is moving forward toward the camera in a natural, species-appropriate way. Use a dramatic low-angle wide-angle perspective with strong depth and perspective distortion. Show the closest {FOREGROUND_BODY_PART} enlarged in the foreground due to perspective, breaking past the bottom edge of the polaroid frame, while keeping the overall pose natural, balanced, and adorable.

Important anatomy rule:
The animal must follow realistic body proportions and species-accurate anatomy. Keep the head, body, limbs, paws, fins, tail, wings, and facial features natural and believable for a {PET_BREED}. Do not exaggerate, deform, or humanize the body structure. Perspective distortion is allowed ONLY for the single foreground {FOREGROUND_BODY_PART} closest to the camera; the rest of the body must remain anatomically correct, balanced, and realistic.

The background is a {BACKGROUND_THEME}, with bright blue sky, soft white cumulus clouds, warm golden sunlight shining through with subtle sun rays, and flowers, plants, and 1-3 butterflies surrounding the scene. The atmosphere should feel {MOOD}, cute, healing, whimsical, and fairy-tale-like.

Visual style:
- photorealistic
- ultra-detailed species-appropriate fur, skin, feather, or scale texture
- sharp facial features with catchlights in the eyes
- clear whisker, feather, skin, or texture details
- shallow depth of field on the background
- soft natural lighting, warm bright tones

The final image should feel magical, cheerful, heartwarming, and visually charming.
The overall layout works as an iPhone wallpaper, with a strong focal point and balanced negative space top and bottom.

Do NOT include any watermark, seller signature, QR code, platform logo, price tag, verified-badge tick, or extra caption text. The ONLY rendered text is the "{USERNAME}" handle on the polaroid frame.
```

| Symptom | Retry phrase to append |
|---|---|
| Frame replicates real Instagram UI exactly (gradient logo, verified tick) | "Stylize the polaroid frame as a generic social-post layout. No Instagram logo, no verified-badge tick, no exact UI replica." |
| Animal sits inside the frame, body does not break past the edges | "The animal's foreground {FOREGROUND_BODY_PART} must clearly break past the bottom edge of the polaroid frame, exaggerated by extreme wide-angle distortion. The body extends OUT of the frame toward the viewer." |
| Anatomy distortion spreads beyond the foreground limb | "Wide-angle distortion applies ONLY to the single foreground {FOREGROUND_BODY_PART}. Head, torso, and other limbs must remain anatomically correct for a {PET_BREED}." |
| Spurious headline / hashtags / extra text | "Remove all rendered text except the single '{USERNAME}' handle on the polaroid frame." |
| Aspect renders square or landscape | "The output must be portrait vertical iPhone wallpaper, 2:3 to 9:16 aspect, NOT square." |
| Background is flat or missing flowers / butterflies | "Restore the fairy-tale background band: blue sky with cumulus clouds, warm sun rays, flowers flanking the frame, 1-3 butterflies." |

presets.template:
# Illustrated Icon Timeline Poster Template

Derived by triangulating three preview images from the Promptbase listing "Illustrated Icon Timeline Posters" by @ssdesgins. Source: `triangulation.json`. Format: prose with verbatim invariant quotes.

## Required invariants (verbatim, reproduce in every prompt)

1. 1:1 square poster. Output size 1024x1024 PNG.
2. Aged / textured watercolor paper background with visible grain, stains, and worn deckled edges.
3. Hand-drawn watercolor + ink rendering: loose ink outlines, watercolor wash, crosshatching, smudges, imperfect handmade edges.
4. Central portrait of the subject, identity-locked to `{PORTRAIT_SUBJECT}`, preserving recognizable facial structure, hair, expression, proportions, and period-appropriate clothing.
5. Hand-lettered display headline at the top of the canvas carrying `{HEADLINE_NAME}` verbatim, in chunky hand-drawn caps with a subtle drop shadow.
6. 4 to 6 dated timeline icons / event callouts arranged around the portrait. Each item from `{TIMELINE_ITEMS}` becomes a hand-sketched watercolor wash + ink outline icon carrying its year and label verbatim, with the visual sketch guided by its sketch hint.
7. 2 to 4 small hand-written equations or diagram annotations from `{FORMULA_ANNOTATIONS}` in negative space, period- and domain-appropriate to `{PORTRAIT_SUBJECT}`.
8. Decorative arrows / dashed lines / spark lines / underline strokes threading the composition.
9. Muted earth-tone palette guided by `{ERA_PALETTE}` accented with `{ACCENT_COLOR}` on energy marks, washes, underlines, and icon highlights.
10. Absolutely no QR codes, no prices, no Promptbase watermark, no @handle text, no seller marks, no marketplace artifacts. Every label, year, and the headline rendered verbatim.

## Variable slots

| Slot | Type | Default | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `HEADLINE_NAME` | string, 1-3 words | — | yes | Verbatim display title rendered in chunky hand-lettered caps. Observed: NIKOLA TESLA, SERENA WILLIAMS, ELON MUSK. |
| `PORTRAIT_SUBJECT` | string | — | yes | Exact person to identity-lock in the central portrait. Observed: Nikola Tesla, Serena Williams, Elon Musk. |
| `ERA_PALETTE` | string, prose color guidance | — | yes | Period / domain palette. Observed bands: sepia + electric blue (Tesla), purple + golden yellow (Williams), graphite + burnt red (Musk). |
| `ACCENT_COLOR` | string | — | yes | One dominant period-appropriate accent for energy marks, washes, underlines, icon highlights. |
| `TIMELINE_ITEMS` | array of `{year, label, sketch_hint}` (4 to 6 entries) | — | yes | Each becomes a hand-sketched watercolor + ink icon around the portrait. `year` and `label` render verbatim; `sketch_hint` guides the glyph drawn. |
| `FORMULA_ANNOTATIONS` | array of strings (2 to 4 entries) | — | yes | Short equations, diagrams, or note-fragments placed in negative space. STEM = math/physics; athletes = stat tallies; engineers = schematic fragments. |

## Prompt skeleton

<!-- format: prose -->

```
For gpt-image-2 at high quality, create a "1:1 square poster" on an "aged/textured watercolor paper background" with visible grain, stains, worn deckled edges, and analog paper texture. Use "hand-drawn watercolor+ink rendering" with loose ink outlines, watercolor wash, crosshatching, smudges, and imperfect handmade edges. Build a "central portrait of the subject (identity-locked)": the face must be an identity-locked face match to {PORTRAIT_SUBJECT}, preserving recognizable facial structure, expression, hair, proportions, and period-appropriate clothing without generic substitution. Place a "hand-lettered display title at top with subject's name": render {HEADLINE_NAME} verbatim in hand-lettered chunky display caps with a subtle drop shadow at the top of the canvas. Arrange "4-6 dated timeline icons / event callouts arranged around the portrait"; each item from {TIMELINE_ITEMS} must become a hand-sketched watercolor wash + ink outline icon carrying {TIMELINE_ITEMS[i].year} and {TIMELINE_ITEMS[i].label} verbatim, with the visual sketch guided by {TIMELINE_ITEMS[i].sketch_hint}. Add "small hand-written equations or formulas as decorative annotations": include 2-4 hand-written formula or diagram annotations from {FORMULA_ANNOTATIONS} in the negative spaces, such as small equations, sine curves, force diagrams, domain diagrams, or period-appropriate notes tied to {PORTRAIT_SUBJECT}. Thread the composition with "decorative arrows / dashed lines / spark lines connecting items", including ink arrows, dashed connector lines, underline strokes, and spark accents. Use a "muted earth-tone palette with one to two accent colors" based on {ERA_PALETTE}, accented with {ACCENT_COLOR} as the period-appropriate highlight. Enforce "no marketplace watermark": absolutely no QR codes, no prices, no Promptbase watermark, no @handle text, no seller marks, and no marketplace artifacts. Text accuracy: every label, year, and the headline rendered verbatim.
```

## How to splice TIMELINE_ITEMS and FORMULA_ANNOTATIONS

The skeleton uses `{TIMELINE_ITEMS[i].year}` and `{TIMELINE_ITEMS[i].label}` as a placeholder for an iterated list. When assembling the engine prompt, expand the list inline before sending. Example for a 4-event timeline:

```
... each item must become a hand-sketched watercolor wash + ink outline icon carrying its year and label verbatim:
  - "1867" "Born in Warsaw" sketched as a Warsaw map pin with a small Polish red-white ribbon,
  - "1898" "Discovers Radium" sketched as a glowing radium sample tube marked Ra,
  - "1903" "Nobel Prize in Physics" sketched as a Nobel medal beside an electroscope,
  - "1911" "Nobel Prize in Chemistry" sketched as a lab flask with an atom diagram.
```

Same pattern for `FORMULA_ANNOTATIONS`: replace the `{FORMULA_ANNOTATIONS}` placeholder with a comma-separated quoted list of the 2-4 annotation strings.

## Failure-mode notes from the three source previews

- The headline is sometimes rendered in the **lower** center (Musk preview) instead of the top (Tesla, Williams). Default to top per invariant 5; if the user wants the lower-center placement, mention it explicitly in the splice.
- Athletes carry far more **all-caps callouts** ("GOAT", "UNSTOPPABLE!") than scientists. These are not invariants; treat them as optional extra FORMULA_ANNOTATIONS entries.
- The Musk preview has a faint pseudo-signature scribble near the bottom that is illegible. This is a stylistic artifact, not part of the template; do not request a signature in the prompt.

presets.template:
# Maximalist Collage Page Template

Source: Promptbase listing "Maximalist Collage Page Creators" by @acb (paywalled, 9 previews triangulated).

## Required invariants (verbatim — reproduce in every prompt)

1. **2:3 portrait aspect.** Output 1024×1536 px (Higgsfield gpt_image_2 portrait) or matched aspect on fallback.
2. **One single-page magazine/scrapbook composition.** Treat the canvas as one editorial page, not a spread, not a poster series.
3. **One dominant headline {HEADLINE}, 1–3 words, ALL CAPS,** placed in the top third, set in a typeface keyed to the theme (slab serif / display serif / chrome serif / typewriter / ransom-note collage / red script / bold sans, picked from `palettes.md`). Always rendered crisp and legible — text accuracy is non-negotiable.
4. **4–9 photographic cut-outs of {HERO_PHOTOS}** scattered across the page, every cut-out showing visible scissor borders or torn-paper edges, never clean rectangles. No single hero — the page IS the hero.
5. **3–6 sub-labels {CALLOUT_1}…{CALLOUT_N}, 1–3 words each,** in a mix of at least two type registers from this set: typewriter, cursive ink, sticker, vintage stencil, ransom-cut, hand-stamped, hand-painted display script. The mix carries the era of the theme.
6. **Aged paper substrate {SUBSTRATE}** — kraft / manila / parchment / velvet / blueprint grid / pulp magazine / corkboard / chalkboard. Never pure white, never a flat solid. Visible grain, scuff, fold, stain, or fiber.
7. **All photos and labels tilted -8° to +8°,** controlled chaos. Nothing axis-aligned.
8. **Themed palette band {PALETTE}** — pick one mood band (3 dominant colors + 1 accent) from `palettes.md` and lock the entire page to it.
9. **Decorative ephemera (pick 2–4 categories per page from {EPHEMERA_SET}):** masking tape strips, postage stamps, ticket stubs, "Nº" catalog numerals, hand-drawn arrows, paperclips, stitching, wax seals, paint splatter, dried-leaf silhouettes, blueprint grid lines.
10. **Cursive handwritten annotations** layered over or alongside photos — short phrases (1–4 words), in pen ink, tilted, occasionally underlined.
11. **No white margin, no clean grid, no QR codes, no seller signature.** No "@PROMPTBASE" or "@acb" watermark. The page bleeds to all four edges.
12. **Text accuracy** — quote {HEADLINE} and every callout slot verbatim in the prompt. No invented words, no garbled type.

## Variable slots

| Slot | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| {THEME} | string | — | required (e.g. "Botany", "Punk Rock", "Cybersecurity") |
| {HEADLINE} | string, 1–3 words ALL CAPS | usually equals {THEME} | required |
| {HERO_PHOTOS} | list of 4–9 subjects | — | required; realistic photographic subjects appropriate to theme |
| {CALLOUTS} | list of 3–6 1–3 word sub-labels | — | required |
| {PALETTE} | enum from `palettes.md` | mood-matched to theme | required if no theme override |
| {SUBSTRATE} | enum (kraft, manila, parchment, velvet, blueprint, pulp, corkboard, chalkboard) | mood-matched | required |
| {TYPE_MIX} | enum-pair from `palettes.md` | mood-matched | required |
| {EPHEMERA_SET} | list of 2–4 from {tape, stamp, ticket, Nº, arrow, paperclip, stitching, wax-seal, splatter, dried-leaf, grid} | mood-matched | required |

## Prompt skeleton

> A maximalist single-page magazine collage on a {SUBSTRATE} substrate, 2:3 portrait aspect, themed around "{THEME}". The dominant headline "{HEADLINE}" is set in {TYPE_MIX_PRIMARY} across the top third in ALL CAPS, large and crisp. Across the page are {HERO_COUNT} photographic cut-outs of {HERO_PHOTOS}, each with visible scissor or torn-paper edges, tilted between -8° and +8°. Layered on and around the photos are sub-labels — {CALLOUTS} — rendered in a mix of {TYPE_MIX_SECONDARY} (typewriter, cursive ink, sticker, stencil, or ransom-cut as fits the era). Decorative ephemera includes {EPHEMERA_SET}. The palette is locked to {PALETTE}. Cursive handwritten annotations are scattered over or beside photos, in pen ink, short phrases, tilted. The composition is controlled chaos — dense, overlapping, magazine-flat-lay top-down view, but every element legible and intentional. The substrate shows grain, scuff, and fold. The page bleeds to all four edges with no white margin, no clean grid, no QR codes, and no watermarks of any kind. Every rendered word — headline and labels — must be spelled correctly and clearly readable.

## Anchor map (rough zones, not rigid)

```
+----------------------------------+
|  ███████ HEADLINE ████████      |   top third — dominant headline
|  ▔▔▔▔▔▔▔▔▔▔▔▔▔▔▔▔▔▔▔▔▔▔        |
|  [photo] [tape]   [photo]       |
|       [callout]  [photo]        |   middle third — densest layering
|   [photo]  ✎ cursive note       |
|        [stamp] [Nº 0042]        |
|  [photo] [callout]  [photo]     |
|     ✎ note   [ticket stub]      |   bottom third — ephemera + sign-off
|  [callout]   [arrow]→ [photo]   |
+----------------------------------+
```

The map is suggestive, not prescriptive. The model should improvise within the chaos rule (-8° to +8° tilt, scissor edges, mixed type registers).

# Premium 3D Corporate UI Posters Template

> Fidelity is locked. Enhancement is a separate, explicit request after acceptance.

## Unanimous structural invariants

1. Square infographic hierarchy with a large top headline, a central 3D hero, surrounding cards, and bottom utility bands (4/4 previews)
2. Dark topic-colored field with bright dimensional accents and white or warm high-contrast typography (4/4 previews)
3. Multiple short actionable tips are organized as a coherent visual system rather than free-floating labels (4/4 previews)

## Discriminative signatures

### Large molded, extruded 3D headline lettering with a chunky numeric lead-in
- Evidence: preview-01.png, preview-02.png, preview-03.png, preview-04.png (4/4 previews)
- Discriminative weight: 5/5
- Prompt clause: large molded extruded 3D headline lettering with a chunky numeric lead-in
- Medium/process/substrate: high-gloss 3D product illustration · soft studio render with beveled extruded type · dark matte digital poster field
- Irregularity: not marked purposeful
- Composition exception: The headline may wrap asymmetrically to preserve large readable letterforms.

### A tangible, polished central hero object anchors the dashboard instead of a flat icon
- Evidence: preview-01.png, preview-02.png, preview-03.png, preview-04.png (4/4 previews)
- Discriminative weight: 5/5
- Prompt clause: a tangible polished central hero object
- Medium/process/substrate: 3D toy-like product render · rounded geometry, controlled specular highlights, soft contact shadows · integrated into the dark poster field
- Irregularity: not marked purposeful
- Composition exception: Hero scale may grow into the mid-frame when it remains clear of cards and headline.

### Rounded glassy dark UI cards with fine bright outlines, numbered badge discs, and miniature dimensional icons
- Evidence: preview-01.png, preview-02.png, preview-03.png, preview-04.png (4/4 previews)
- Discriminative weight: 5/5

### Wide lower PRO TIP callout bar plus a compact icon-and-label footer navigation strip

## Variable slots

# Premium Viral Fact Designs Template

## Required invariants (verbatim — reproduce in every prompt)

1. 1:1 square editorial social fact card. Output size 1024×1024 PNG.
2. Five-zone hierarchy only: headline block, one hero illustration, one dominant fact panel, one compact icon-led support strip, one decorative footer strip.
3. Oversized stacked DID YOU KNOW? headline with bold clean editorial typography; no messy sketch lettering.
4. Prominent right-side or upper-right hero illustration with clean silhouette, correct z-order, and purposeful overlap; prefer simple objects, charts, planets, clouds, landmarks, organs, or clean mascots over complex tentacled/limbed creatures unless requested.
5. Hero rendering is polished flat-vector/editorial with controlled geometry, not sketchy, scribbly, scratchy, painterly, faux-hand-drawn, or over-doodled.
6. One large main fact statement with a single accent-emphasized keyword or statistic; do not split the main fact into several competing headlines.
7. Modular cards and badges are restrained: maximum one speech bubble, one stat badge, one support strip, and three bottom icon tiles.
8. Bottom support area is icon-led: bottom tiles use pictograms plus 1–3 word labels only; no sentences, no dense captions, no tiny body copy.
9. Footer strip is a decorative ribbon by default; if text is used, it must be 1–3 words only.
10. Bold readable display typography paired with sparse body copy; every generated text surface must be large enough to read at social-feed thumbnail size.
11. Playful educational editorial vector style with thick intentional outlines, clean filled shapes, limited texture, and topic-specific icons; no weird sketch style.
12. Themed decorative background supports the fact but never becomes a generic gradient, particle field, cluttered AI collage, or sketchbook page.
13. Premium human-designed fact-card composition: visible margins, aligned panels, consistent icon system, clear hierarchy, and no filler ornament.
14. No watermark, no seller signature, no QR codes, no price tags, no marketplace artifacts.
15. Text accuracy: quote {MAIN_FACT}, {PRIMARY_CALLOUT}, {STAT_BADGE}, and support labels verbatim; include {FOOTER_TAGLINE} only when non-empty; reject duplicated headings or hallucinated extra labels.
16. Anti-slop: no sketchy mascot anatomy, no tentacle/limb weirdness, no overstuffed bottom text, no generic AI infographic gloss, no overstuffed panel soup, no meaningless detail clusters, no fake UI glyphs, no inconsistent shadows, no broken occlusion, no mushy vector edges.

```text

Theme and background: {BACKGROUND}; use {PALETTE} with strong accent contrast, subtle paper grain or print texture, visible margins, and only a few topic-relevant decorative marks. Use a strict five-zone composition: (1) top headline block, (2) prominent right-side hero, (3) one dominant left/center fact panel, (4) one compact icon-led support strip, (5) bottom footer strip. Headline: oversized stacked DID YOU / KNOW? in clean bold uppercase editorial display typography in the top area, two-tone emphasis, clean alignment, and no duplicate headline elsewhere. Do not use messy sketch lettering. Hero: place one prominent right-side or upper-right {HERO_SUBJECT}; render it as polished flat editorial vector artwork with clean filled shapes, thick controlled outlines, smooth intentional curves, correct z-order, consistent shadow direction, and no sketchy/scribbly contour lines. Avoid weird anatomy, tentacle/limb tangles, lumpy mascot deformation, mushy contact points, or meaningless surface details. Main fact: create one large rounded left/center information panel containing exactly {MAIN_FACT}; make one key word, subject, or statistic oversized and accent-colored. Add one rounded speech bubble or kicker near the hero containing exactly {PRIMARY_CALLOUT}. Add one compact stat badge reading exactly {STAT_BADGE}. Add one horizontal support strip with exactly 3 short labels reading exactly {PROCESS_OR_COMPARISON}; each label must be 1–3 words, poster-scale, and paired with a simple consistent pictogram. Along the bottom, place three compact decorative icon tiles with simple pictograms only. If {SUPPORTING_FACT_1}, {SUPPORTING_FACT_2}, or {SUPPORTING_FACT_3} are non-empty, use them as 1–2 word labels; if they are empty, keep the icon tiles textless. Never duplicate the support-strip labels in the bottom tiles and never add sentence microcopy. Finish with one rounded decorative footer strip/banner. If {FOOTER_TAGLINE} is non-empty, place it large and clean as a 1–3 word label; if {FOOTER_TAGLINE} is empty, use the footer as a textless decorative color band. Do not add CTA slogans or extra bottom microcopy. Optional explainer copy may appear only if it fits as one short sentence in the dominant fact panel: {EXPLAINER_COPY}. ```

Reject and retry if the output has any of these:

- Weird sketch style: scribbly contour lines, scratchy mascot rendering, faux-hand-drawn anatomy, or lumpy AI character deformation.
- Complex tentacled/limbed mascot failure: tangled limbs, strange suckers/fingers, mushy contact points, or unclear silhouette.
- Bottom text that reads like AI microcopy: sentences in mini cards, CTA slogans, tiny captions, pseudo-English, or text that only looks plausible from a distance.
- More than five major content zones or a cluttered “panel soup” layout.
- Duplicate `DID YOU KNOW?` headlines, hallucinated captions, lorem text, fake UI labels, or random glyph badges.
- Generic glossy AI vector look: meaningless sparkles, random blob gradients, oversmoothed mascot, inconsistent shadows, broken z-order, or mushy outlines.
- Too many competing facts; the card must have one dominant fact and three short support labels.
- Watermark, QR code, price, seller handle, marketplace artifact, extremist symbol, armband, dictator likeness, Axis/Soviet regalia.

- Rationale: a simple planet/chart hero avoids octopus tentacle anatomy and a textless footer plus textless bottom pictograms avoids CTA and repeated-label microcopy.

10. No watermark, no `@` handles, no QR codes, no price tags, no seller signature, no marketplace UI, no borders, no spurious extra text, no alternate view-label wording (no `FRONT VIEW`, no `45-DEGREE VIEW`).

View order and labels: from left to right render front, left side, right side, back, and 45 angle. Center a small sans-serif uppercase label beneath each figure at 10-13 pt. Use only these literal callouts in this exact order: "FRONT", "LEFT SIDE", "RIGHT SIDE", "BACK", "45 ANGLE".

# Template: Gamedev 3D Character Sheets

Source: Promptbase listing "Gamedev 3D Character Sheets" by @lostmighty.
Format (per template-extraction-rubric.md Pass 6): **prose**. Character art benefits from coherent prose more than JSON-spec; the three-figure invariant is preserved by explicit positional language.

Aspect ratio: **3:2 landscape**, generated at `1536x1024` on gpt-image-2.

## Invariants

These appear in every preview and must appear in every generation. Verbatim.

1. Three full-body 3D character views arranged horizontally in a single row.
2. View order: front, three-quarter side, back (left-to-right).
3. Stylized 3D-render aesthetic, AAA-video-game character-art quality, hand-painted PBR textures.
4. Identical character preserved across all three views (same proportions, outfit, hair, accessories, palette).
5. Static neutral stance (T-pose-adjacent), arms relaxed at sides, weight balanced.
6. Clean white-to-light-grey vertical gradient background, no environment, no horizon, no props beyond what the character wears or holds.
7. Soft contact shadow on the ground beneath each figure.
8. Soft key light from upper-front, cool subtle fill, gentle ambient occlusion.
9. All three figures the same height, eye level matched, even horizontal spacing.
10. No text, no labels, no watermarks, no panel borders, no captions.
11. Wide landscape 3:2 composition.

## Variable slots

| Name | Type | Default | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `{CHARACTER_DESCRIPTION}` | prose, 5-15 words | — | yes | Species, gender or build, archetype, age band. E.g. "young female elven ranger". |
| `{OUTFIT}` | prose, 5-20 words | — | yes | Materials, colors, layers. E.g. "forest-green leather armor over a linen tunic, brown belt and boots". |
| `{HAIR}` | prose, 3-10 words | — | yes | Color, length, style. E.g. "long auburn braid". |
| `{ACCESSORIES_CLAUSE}` | prose, prefixed with ", and " or empty string | "" | no | Held props or worn accessories. E.g. ", and a quiver of feathered arrows on her back plus a dagger sheathed at her hip". |
| `{IDENTITY_NOTE}` | prose or empty | "" | no | Optional identity-lock language when the user supplies a photo or specific character reference. E.g. " The character's face matches the reference photo exactly." |

Slot value rules:
- All slots are prose fragments, not bullet lists or JSON.
- `{ACCESSORIES_CLAUSE}` is the only slot that includes its own grammatical glue. When empty, leave the surrounding sentence intact.
- Do not introduce environment, scenery, or background slots. The background invariant is non-negotiable.

## Prompt skeleton

The verbatim engine input for gpt-image-2. Substitute slots only; do not rewrite the invariant clauses.

```
A character turnaround sheet for a video game asset, rendered as three full-body 3D character views arranged horizontally in a single row: front view on the left, three-quarter side view in the center, back view on the right. The character is {CHARACTER_DESCRIPTION}, wearing {OUTFIT}, with {HAIR}{ACCESSORIES_CLAUSE}.{IDENTITY_NOTE}

Style: high-quality stylized 3D rendering in the manner of modern AAA video-game character concept art, Pixar-meets-Riot Games aesthetic, clean topology, hand-painted PBR textures, crisp silhouette readable at small size.

All three poses are static neutral T-pose-adjacent stances, arms relaxed at sides, weight balanced. The character is perfectly identical across all three angles: same proportions, same outfit details, same hair, same props, same color palette. No alternate outfits, no variants, no progressions.

Lighting: soft key light from upper-front, cool subtle fill, gentle ambient occlusion, soft contact shadow on the ground under each figure.

Background: plain white-to-light-grey vertical gradient with no environment, no horizon, no scenery, no props beyond what the character is wearing or holding.

Composition: characters fill the vertical extent of the frame with small top and bottom margin, even horizontal spacing between the three views, all three figures the same height and at the same eye level.

Absolutely no text, no labels, no watermarks, no captions, no panel borders, no UI overlays.

Wide landscape 3:2 composition suitable for use as a character reference sheet for a 3D modeler or game artist.
```

## Self-test demo subject

presets.template:
# Pixel Art PFP

> **Higgsfield image selector:** For Higgsfield still-image model choice, model shootouts, credit-sensitive image calls, or still keyframes before video, load `higgsfield-image-generation-playbook` first, then the narrow specialist.

Reusable skill for cute pixel-art profile pictures that match the Promptbase **Pixel Art Profile Pictures 2** template by `@tinyprompts` (recommended model: GPT-4o / `gpt-image-2`, intended for social-media avatars, ~40-word base prompt). Use it any time the user wants a pixel avatar, sprite-style headshot, retro-game profile picture, chibi pixel portrait, or anything described as "that tinyprompts pixel pfp style".

## Required signal

Proceed once the user has provided **at least one** of:

- A character description (subject, hair, accessories, vibe), OR
- A face photo to convert (attach inline or by path)

If the user attaches a face photo, label it explicitly:
- `edit target` — pixel-ify *this* face, preserve recognizable features (skin tone, hair color/length, glasses, beard, hat). Use the **edit** path.
- `subject reference` — match identity but generate fresh. Use the **generate** path with description derived from the photo.

If the user asks for a **set** ("make me 5 pfps", "give me variants"), produce N images by issuing one generation call per pfp. Do **not** use `n` as a substitute for distinct pfps — each call gets the same skeleton with one slot varied (palette, accessory, mood).

## Generation backend (hard rules)

Default backend is **`gpt-image-2`** through the existing `imagegen` skill (built-in `image_gen` tool). Do not silently downgrade. The full model-selection rules from `imagegen` apply here verbatim.

Two backends are supported:

1. **`imagegen` (default).** Built-in `image_gen` tool, `model=gpt-image-2`, `quality=high`, size `1024x1024` (1:1 square — pfps are always square).
2. **Higgsfield MCP fallback.** Only when (a) the user explicitly asks for Higgsfield, (b) `imagegen` errors and the user authorizes the fallback, or (c) the user wants the same prompt fanned across multiple Higgsfield models for comparison. Use `model: gpt_image_2` only — never the older `gpt_image`. If `gpt_image_2` errors, surface the error, do not downgrade. Read `sources/higgsfield/guide.md` first if not already read this session.

Never invent a third backend. Never silently route to a different model.

## Required template invariants

Every generated pfp MUST satisfy these. Repeat them verbatim in the prompt. They are the contract that makes the output match the template:

1. **Square 1:1 avatar.** Output `1024x1024`. No portrait/landscape crops. The image must be readable as a profile picture when masked into a circle by social-media UIs (keep important detail away from the four corners).
2. **Pixel-art rendering, not pixel-art-styled illustration.** The output is a low-resolution sprite (visually equivalent to a 64x64 to 128x128 sprite) **upscaled with strict nearest-neighbor**. Every visible edge aligns to the pixel grid. **No anti-aliasing across grid cells. No motion blur. No painterly soft edges. No gaussian shading.** Hand-placed dithering (checker, ordered) is allowed inside shading transitions; flat planes stay flat.
3. **Centered chibi headshot.** Head + shoulders bust, head occupies roughly 55-70% of frame height, eyes on the upper-third line. Slightly oversized head, simplified expressive features (large eyes, small nose dot, small mouth). Forward-facing or 3/4 turn. Subject is not cropped at the top of the head.
4. **Limited vibrant palette.** 8-16 total colors per character. High saturation. Soft outline at 1-2px in a *darker shade of the adjacent fill* (not pure black). Two-tone or three-tone shading per surface (base + shadow + optional highlight). Skin tones use 3 shades.
5. **Flat solid background.** One uniform color block (no gradient ramp, no photoreal scene, no bokeh) chosen to complement the character palette (use a contrasting hue from the opposite side of the wheel, or a muted neutral). Optional: a sparse decorative pixel motif — small stars, dots, hearts, tiny clouds, or a single vignette frame — placed away from the head and shoulders. **No scenery, no environment, no text inside the background.**
6. **No text, no watermark, no signature, no logos, no UI chrome, no border frame.** This template ships clean. The Promptbase previews carry no text; do not add any.
7. **Identity preservation (edit path only).** When converting a real face photo, preserve: skin tone, hair color + length + style, facial hair, glasses (frame shape + color), hat or headwear, signature accessory (earrings, necklace visible at shoulders), expression. Do **not** preserve: background, clothing detail beyond shoulder line, blemishes, exact pose. Stylize the rest into the template.

If the user requests a deviation (e.g., "full-body sprite", "transparent background", "add my username under the avatar"), honor it, but flag that the output will deviate from the canonical template.

## Workflow

1. **Decide the path.**
   - No photo, or photo as `subject reference` → **generate** path.
   - Photo as `edit target` → **edit** path. Built-in `image_gen` edit mode requires the image to be in conversation context. If the photo is a local file, load it with `view_image` first (per the `imagegen` skill rules).
2. **Collect the inputs** (do not invent):
   - Subject: pronouns, age band (kid / teen / adult), skin tone, hair (color, length, style), eye color, distinguishing features (freckles, beard, glasses).
   - Accessories: hat, headphones, earrings, scarf, hoodie, etc.
   - Vibe / role flavor: cozy, cyberpunk, witchy, dev, gamer, athlete, retro 90s, etc. (optional)
   - Background color preference, or `auto` (pick a complement to the dominant character color).
   - Decorative motif: `none` / `stars` / `hearts` / `dots` / `sparkles` / `arcade` / `pet`.
3. **Assemble the final prompt** from the skeleton in the next section. Keep invariants verbatim. Customize only the slots.
4. **Generate** via the chosen backend:
   - `imagegen` default: built-in `image_gen` tool, `gpt-image-2`, `quality=high`, size `1024x1024`. One call per pfp.
   - Higgsfield: MCP image generation tool, `model: gpt_image_2`, `aspect: 1:1`.
5. **Validate the output** against every invariant. Specifically check:
   - Crisp pixel grid with no anti-aliased fringe (zoom in mentally on the silhouette edge — it should be staircase-stepped, not feathered).
   - Square 1:1 with the head safely inside the central circle (so it survives a circular avatar mask).
   - Flat solid background, no gradient, no scene.
   - No text, no watermark.
   - For edit path: identity features preserved per the list above.
6. **If a check fails**, retry once with one targeted correction in the prompt (e.g., "the silhouette must be true nearest-neighbor pixel art, not vector cartoon — every edge stair-steps along the grid"). Do not loop more than twice without surfacing the issue to the user.
7. **Persist + render.** Save the final image to the session `data/` folder (or to a project path if the user named one). Render with an `image-preview` block pointing at the saved file. State the model, size, and backend used (e.g., `model=gpt-image-2 quality=high size=1024x1024 backend=imagegen`).

## Iteration

For follow-up changes ("make the background mint instead of coral", "add round glasses", "switch to 3/4 turn"), reuse the assembled prompt and change exactly the named slot. **Repeat all invariants every iteration** so the model does not drift back to soft-shaded vector cartoon (the most common failure mode).

For a multi-pfp set, fan out one call per pfp with the same skeleton and per-pfp inputs. Render the set as a single `image-preview` block with `items` (one tab per pfp) so the user can flip between them.

## Prompt skeleton (fill the slots, keep everything else verbatim)

```

rendered as a low-resolution sprite (equivalent to a 96x96 sprite) upscaled with strict nearest-neighbor — every edge stair-steps along the pixel grid, NO anti-aliasing across grid cells, NO soft painterly edges, NO gaussian blur, NO motion blur.

# Minimalist Movie Poster Template

Triangulated from 9 public previews of Promptbase listing "Minimalist Movie Posters" (@promptstudio, gpt-image-2 family, paywalled). Format: layout-as-prompt.

Visual lineage (hard anchor): **Saul Bass title-card minimalism, Polish poster school, Olly Moss / Mondo alternative movie posters.** Screen-print and vector, not illustration.

## Required invariants (verbatim — reproduce in every prompt)

1. Portrait 2:3 vertical poster. Output size 1024×1536 PNG.
2. Every color region is a single solid flat color fill, separated from neighboring regions by a hard boolean edge. No interior gradient inside any region. No airbrush, no soft shading, no rendered volume, no implied 3D.
3. 2 to 4 solid colors in the entire poster, including the background. Palette is mood-coupled to the film concept.
4. One or two iconic hero subjects framed bust-up or 3/4 length, built from at most 3 to 4 flat color regions per subject (e.g. silhouette, lit skin region, shadow skin region, hair shape). Where lit and shadow regions meet on the same subject, the boundary is a hard straight or hard curved edge, not a gradient.
5. Large film-title typography in one clearly reserved title bar at top or bottom. Title bar is flat, single-color, with the title rendered in a contrasting flat fill. Bold geometric or condensed sans-serif by default; serif italic only when the supplied title clearly calls for it (e.g., very feminine or whimsical concept).
6. One secondary iconic prop or symbol, integrated into the composition. Built from the same flat-fill / hard-boolean-edge rules. Never a separate text block.
7. Background is one solid flat color field (atmospheric layers like a starfield, concentric arcs, or distant skyline are allowed only if they are themselves flat shapes with no internal modulation).
8. No watermark, no QR code, no price tag, no marketplace artifact, no tagline, no extra subtitles, no credits.

## Hard banned terms / techniques (do not allow into the rendered image)

**Rendering / style band:** cel-shading, rendered volume, soft shading, airbrush, implied 3D, digital painting, illustration with internal modulation, photorealism, gradient, vignette, lens flare, lighting falloff, hair strands, fabric texture, skin texture, stippling, cross-hatching, halftone (unless the user explicitly asks), pencil rendering, watercolor wash, noise grain, film grain, drop shadow inside a shape, glow inside a shape.

**Identity / safety band (always required, regardless of palette or film):** no resemblance to any real-world political, military, or religious figure of the 20th or 21st century — explicitly including, but not limited to, Adolf Hitler, Joseph Stalin, Benito Mussolini, Francisco Franco, Mao Zedong, Pol Pot, Saddam Hussein, Kim Il-sung, Kim Jong-il, Kim Jong-un, Osama bin Laden, Donald Trump, Vladimir Putin, Xi Jinping, the British royal family, or any sitting or recent head of state. No party uniforms, no military regalia of any specific real-world regime, no armbands, no propaganda salutes, no swastikas, no hammer-and-sickle, no fasces, no Confederate iconography, no Klan robes, no flag emblems of contested or extremist movements. Hero faces are generic and iconic — never modeled on a specific real person. If the source film features identifiable actors, render the role-archetype (e.g., "young Brad-Pitt-era charismatic-anarchist archetype" → "a stylized confident male figure with messy hair") rather than the actor's likeness.

**Palette-driven failure-mode guard:** the combination of red background + black silhouette + cream / yellow title + stern centered male portrait + bold sans-serif title strongly evokes 1930s European propaganda posters in the model's training distribution. When this palette is selected, the model must double down on the identity / safety band above and visibly stylize the figure (face split, abstract silhouette, profile, exaggerated geometric features) so the result cannot be mistaken for a propaganda portrait. Add at least one disqualifying stylization: extreme face split, profile-only view, mask, eye-bar, or replace the face entirely with an iconic object (per the abstract-preferred guidance below).

| Slot | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| {TITLE} | string, exact rendered movie title | — | required. Render exactly as supplied; preserve case, punctuation, numbers, diacritics. Tell the model to leave a comfortable horizontal margin on both sides of the title so no letter is clipped at the canvas edge. |
| {HERO_SUBJECT} | string description | — | required. One iconic figure, paired figures, or compact scene. Must read clearly at poster scale and decompose into 3 to 4 flat color regions. |

| {PALETTE_PRIMARY} | color token or short palette phrase | — | required. Dominant subject / foreground color. One named color, not a range. |
| {PALETTE_ACCENT} | color token or short palette phrase | — | required. Title / highlight / symbolic accent color. One named color. |
| {PALETTE_BG} | color token or short palette phrase | — | required. Flat poster background field color. One named color. |
| {TITLE_POSITION} | enum: `top` \| `bottom` | `bottom` | required. Use one title bar only, fully contained inside the canvas. |

The result must not be mistakable for a propaganda portrait.

Canvas and color:
The background is a single flat field of {PALETTE_BG}. The dominant subject and foreground shapes are flat fills of {PALETTE_PRIMARY}. The title bar / highlights / symbolic accents are flat fills of {PALETTE_ACCENT}. The total palette across the entire poster is exactly these three colors plus, only if strictly needed for legibility, one neutral (black or cream). Every shape is a solid color region; every boundary between regions is a hard boolean edge.

Abstract-preferred hero guidance (read first):
The Saul Bass / Olly Moss / Mondo tradition often replaces a character portrait with an *iconic object*: a single bar of soap (Fight Club), a bowler hat (A Clockwork Orange), a single rose (American Beauty), a glove (Edward Scissorhands), a typewriter (The Shining), a stylized silhouette without facial detail, or a profile-only view with no front-facing features. When {HERO_SUBJECT} describes one or more recognizable real actors or characters, PREFER one of these abstract / iconic / profile-only treatments instead of rendering a front-facing portrait. Place {HERO_SUBJECT} as the main iconic poster subject, framed bust-up or 3/4 length OR as an iconic object filling the same hero slot. Render exactly the string "{TITLE}" in that title bar, with a comfortable horizontal margin on both sides of the canvas so no letter is clipped. Do not paraphrase the title, do not translate it, do not split it into unintended words, do not add subtitles, do not add a tagline. Imagine the result printed as a two-to-four-color silk-screen. If any region in the final image cannot be cleanly separated as a single solid color screen, the image is wrong and must be regenerated as flatter.

# Mixed Media Collage Art Template

Source: Promptbase "Mixed Media Collage Art" by @byteboy1, gpt-image-2.

## Required invariants (verbatim, reproduce in every prompt)

1. **Square 1:1 vertical canvas. Output size 1024×1024 PNG.**
2. **Single hero subject**, centered, occupying 60-85% of the canvas height. Hero-shot framing (close-up to mid-shot). One subject only, no group compositions, no scenes with multiple separate figures.
3. **Hero rendered in fluid black ink and dense crosshatched charcoal**, with bold gestural brushstrokes. The hero looks hand-painted, partially drawn directly onto the underlying paper fragments so the magazine print shows through the figure in places — never a clean cut-out, never a photograph.
4. **Background built from torn and overlapping fragments of vintage luxury-fashion magazine pages.** Required brand fragments to include (rotate at least 6 of these per generation, scattered as torn scraps): `VOGUE`, `Dior`, `CHANEL`, `PRADA`, `YVES SAINT LAURENT` / `SAINT LAURENT` / `YSL`, `LOUIS VUITTON` / `LV`, `GUCCI`, `BALENCIAGA`, `CARTIER`, `HARPER'S BAZAAR` / `BAZAAR`, `CHANEL N°5`, `GIVENCHY`, `CÉLINE`, `TOM FORD`. Logos appear in their real serif typography. Paper is aged cream-to-yellow, visibly creased, with torn raw edges and faint drop-shadowed tape strips.
5. **Exactly ONE saturated color accent in the entire frame** — every other surface stays monochrome charcoal/off-white/black. The accent is the focal device and must read instantly. The accent is `{ACCENT_COLOR}` and it tints `{ACCENT_TARGET}` (a specific part of the hero or a small landscape inside a reflective surface).
6. **Magazine serif typography reads through the collage.** VOGUE-style display caps, Dior italic serif, CHANEL spaced caps are part of the background. The hero overlaps that typography; do not redraw the typography over the hero.
7. **Optional editorial pull-quote slot `{PULL_QUOTE}`** — one short line in serif italics set into the collage (e.g., "Elegance is refusal", "FASHION CHANGES BUT STYLE ENDURES", "I DON'T DO FASHION I AM FASHION", "LIVE FAST DRESS WELL"). Default: omit. Include only when the user supplies the line.
8. **Lighting:** flat, painterly, no rendered photographic lighting. Treat the image as a painting on paper, not as a 3D render.
9. **No QR codes, no price tags, no Promptbase signature, no third-party watermark. No real living-person likeness unless the user explicitly names the subject and authorizes it.**
10. **Text accuracy:** when `{PULL_QUOTE}` is provided, render it verbatim in serif italics inside the collage. Magazine brand logos are quoted verbatim from the list above.

## Variable slots

| Slot | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `{HERO_SUBJECT}` | string | — | required; iconic single subject (e.g., "great horned owl perched frontally", "1955 Mercedes 300SL roadster three-quarter front view", "ballerina mid-leap in arabesque") |
| `{ACCENT_COLOR}` | string | — | required; single saturated color (e.g., "cherry red", "cobalt blue", "warm metallic gold", "emerald green", "salmon pink", "amber yellow", "orange-magenta sunset") |
| `{ACCENT_TARGET}` | string | — | required; specific part of the hero or feature that carries the accent (e.g., "steering wheel", "ballet shoes", "guitar body", "leaves of the branch", "eyes", "the reflection inside the helmet visor") |
| `{PULL_QUOTE}` | string | omitted | optional; short serif italic line set inside the collage |

## Prompt skeleton (engine input)

A square 1:1 mixed-media collage artwork in the "Mixed Media Collage Art" style. Output size 1024×1024.

Hero: {HERO_SUBJECT}, centered, occupying about 70% of the canvas, framed as a hero-shot. The hero is rendered in fluid black ink and dense crosshatched charcoal with bold gestural brushstrokes, as if hand-painted directly onto the underlying paper. The hero is monochrome except for one saturated color accent.

Single color accent: a saturated {ACCENT_COLOR} on the {ACCENT_TARGET}. This is the only color in the entire image; every other surface, including the rest of the hero, the magazine fragments, and any incidental detail, stays in black, charcoal, and aged off-white.

Background: a chaotic, hand-torn collage of overlapping fragments from vintage luxury-fashion magazines. Include at least six recognizable serif-typography logos scattered as torn scraps: VOGUE, Dior, CHANEL, PRADA, YVES SAINT LAURENT, LOUIS VUITTON, GUCCI, BALENCIAGA, CARTIER, HARPER'S BAZAAR, CHANEL N°5, GIVENCHY, CÉLINE, TOM FORD. # Modern Poster Designs Template

Source: Promptbase listing "Modern Poster Designs" by @dreamydesigns. Bauhaus-adjacent vertical poster with B&W hero, single saturated color block, bold sans-serif headline.

## Required invariants (verbatim — reproduce in every prompt)

1. **2:3 vertical aspect ratio.** Portrait orientation. Output size 1024×1536 (or matching engine limit, never landscape).
2. **Warm cream paper background.** Off-white #F5EFE3 family, slight warmth. Not pure white. No grain unless explicitly requested.
3. **Headline at top-left.** 1–3 words, bold black sans-serif (Helvetica Bold / Inter Bold / DM Sans Bold equivalent). May break onto 2 lines. Verbatim copy from {HEADLINE}.
4. **Optional dot accent** trailing the headline — small filled black circle the size of a period, sitting on the baseline of the last word, or a literal period if the copy ends in one. On by default; off only when {DOT_ACCENT} is explicitly false.
5. **Thin horizontal hairline rule** below the headline block (full canvas width or just under the headline column — match preview-01 spacing).
6. **One saturated color block** behind the hero. Vertical rectangle, narrower than the canvas (~50–60% canvas width), centered horizontally. Single solid color — no gradient, no texture. Color drawn from {COLOR_BLOCK} (see `palettes.md`).
7. **Hero subject rendered in pure black-and-white** with smooth tonal range. No color tint on the hero itself. The hero is composited in front of the color block and is allowed to protrude above the block top and below the block bottom — silhouette must read cleanly against the cream background where it leaves the block.
8. **Bottom strip** with a thin horizontal hairline rule running the full canvas width above it. Below the rule: {LOCATION} bottom-left in bold black sans (allowed to stack 2 lines like "DAVID BOWIE / IN LONDON"), {YEAR} bottom-right in the same family. Both are verbatim from inputs.
9. **No watermarks, no seller signatures, no QR codes, no price tags, no extra copy** beyond the headline, location, and year.
10. **Text accuracy.** {HEADLINE}, {LOCATION}, and {YEAR} must render exactly as supplied. No autocorrect, no rephrasing, no smart-quotes.

## Variable slots

| Slot | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `{HEADLINE}` | string, 1–3 words | — | required. ALL CAPS or Title Case both valid; default ALL CAPS for landmarks/animals/concepts, Title Case for proper-noun figures. |
| `{HERO_SUBJECT}` | string description or attached reference image | — | required. If attached, append the identity-lock block (see below) so the face/silhouette is preserved. |
| `{COLOR_BLOCK}` | enum from `palettes.md` or hex | category default | required. Pick a saturated single color; mood-match the subject. |
| `{LOCATION}` | string, optional | empty | bottom-left footer. Leave blank for landmark-only posters (preview-01 dropped it). Allowed to stack 2 lines with " / " or newline. |
| `{YEAR}` | string | — | required. 4-digit modern year, era stamp ("130 BC"), or any short date string. |
| `{DOT_ACCENT}` | bool | true | small black circle/period trailing the headline. |

## Identity-lock block (use only when hero is a real person or trademarked subject)

Append to the prompt skeleton:

```
100% identical face match to the reference image.
Strictly preserve: exact facial structure, skin tone (rendered as B&W tonal values),
hairstyle, eye shape, lip shape, jawline, nose proportions, ear shape.
Render the subject in pure monochrome black-and-white photography.
```

Drop this block when the hero is a generic landmark, animal, or non-identity object.

## Prompt skeleton

The single prose block below is the engine input. Fill the slots verbatim, no quotes around them, then send.

> Vertical 2:3 modern minimalist Bauhaus poster on warm cream paper background (#F5EFE3, slightly warm off-white).
>
> Top-left headline: "{HEADLINE}" set in bold black geometric sans-serif (Helvetica Bold / Inter Bold weight), all caps if {HEADLINE} is ≤2 words or describes a landmark/animal/concept, Title Case if it is a proper-noun figure name. Allow the headline to break onto 2 lines if length requires. {DOT_ACCENT_CLAUSE: include "Place a small filled black circle the size of a period immediately after the final word of the headline, sitting on the baseline." when DOT_ACCENT is true; otherwise omit.}
>
> Thin horizontal black hairline rule sits beneath the headline.
>
> Center of canvas: a single solid {COLOR_BLOCK} vertical rectangle, narrower than the canvas (~55% canvas width), centered horizontally, occupying the middle ~60% of canvas height. No gradient, no texture, flat color.
>
> In front of the color block: a high-contrast pure black-and-white {HERO_SUBJECT}, photographic if the subject is real, line illustration if it is an artwork. The hero is allowed to extend above the top edge and below the bottom edge of the color block; the silhouette must read cleanly against the cream paper where it overflows. Hero is rendered in pure monochrome — no color tint at all on the hero itself.
>
> Above the bottom strip: a thin horizontal black hairline rule running the full canvas width.
>
> Bottom-left: "{LOCATION}" in bold black sans-serif at the same family weight as the headline, allowed to stack on 2 lines if a city/context follows the name. {LOCATION_OMIT_CLAUSE: omit this line entirely when {LOCATION} is empty.}
>
> Bottom-right: "{YEAR}" in the same bold black sans.
>
> Generous cream negative space frames the entire composition. No watermark, no signature, no QR code, no price tag, no extra copy. Print-poster aesthetic, gallery-grade typography, Bauhaus minimalism.

## Negation block (append verbatim — fights common GPT-Image-2 failure modes)

> Negative: do not render the hero in color, do not gradient or texture the color block, do not center the headline, do not add any seller watermark, do not invent a fifth body of text, do not add stars or particles, do not change the year.

## How to assemble final prompt

1. Substitute every `{SLOT}` with verbatim user input.
2. Resolve `{DOT_ACCENT_CLAUSE}` and `{LOCATION_OMIT_CLAUSE}` per the rules above.
3. Append the identity-lock block if hero is a real person or trademarked product.
4. Append the negation block verbatim.
5. Send to engine with `model=gpt_image_2`, `quality=high`, `aspect=2:3` (or `1024x1536`).

The skeleton above is what `references/template.md` loads when the skill runs.

# Parametric Poster Systems Template

Reverse-engineered from 5 public previews of the Promptbase listing "Parametric Poster Systems" by @herrartur. Style is a brutalist + Swiss editorial + grunge zine magazine cover, rendered as a *family* of cohesive posters keyed off a single theme.

## Required invariants (verbatim — reproduce in every prompt)

1. **2:3 vertical poster.** Output size 1024×1536 px (or aspect 2:3 native). Magazine-cover format. No alternate aspects.
2. **Massive condensed bold sans-serif display headline**, ALL CAPS, 1-2 words stacked, occupies the upper ~30% of the canvas, edge-to-edge horizontally. Verbatim copy slot {THEME_TITLE} (1-2 words, may be split across two stacked lines).
3. **Two-color duotone palette.** A dark base color {BASE_COLOR} (charcoal, deep navy, or near-black) plus one saturated accent {ACCENT_COLOR} keyed to the theme. Headline and key text are rendered in either the accent or in cream/ivory. No third hue in the palette.
4. **Photographic hero subject {HERO_SUBJECT}** centered in the mid-frame, rendered as a duotone aligned to the palette, with visible halftone-dot grain and slight CMYK misregistration. The hero is a person/figure or scene tied to the theme.
5. **Top-right cluster.** A large {ISSUE_NUMBER} (2-digit number or short date string) in cream/ivory, with three short lines of all-caps editorial micro-copy stacked beside it.
6. **Top-left small bar/badge.** A black or accent-colored bar containing one short stamp word (often the theme name or a single-word mood tag) plus a colored dot or rule.
7. **Vertical small-caps margin text** running along the left and right edges. {MARGIN_TAGLINE} on at least one side. Set in a thin condensed sans-serif at small size.
8. **Mid-left secondary badge.** A solid color block (usually accent) containing a stamp-style logo glyph and 2-3 short lines of all-caps editorial copy {BADGE_COPY}.
9. **Bottom serif-italic-bold sub-caption {SUB_CAPTION}** (1 line) in cream/ivory, optionally followed by a smaller secondary line. Sits across the lower third over or beside the hero.
10. **Bottom strip with editorial microtext**: a tiny barcode-like indicator and an "ISSUE Nº", "VOL. NN / ISSUE NN", or short date in small caps.
11. **Whole-canvas grunge treatment.** Visible film grain, halftone dot pattern, CMYK misregistration, paper-scuff texture, faint dust/scratches. Print-zine fidelity, not clean digital.
12. **Optional secondary-language text {SECONDARY_LANGUAGE_TEXT}** — 1-3 glyphs of kanji, cyrillic, greek, or other non-Latin script set as oversized vertical or stamp-style mark, keyed to theme. Skip cleanly if not relevant.
13. **No watermark, no seller signature, no QR codes, no price tags, no @handle text anywhere on the canvas.**
14. **Text accuracy.** Quote {THEME_TITLE}, {ISSUE_NUMBER}, {SUB_CAPTION}, {BADGE_COPY}, and {MARGIN_TAGLINE} verbatim in the prompt.

## Variable slots

| Slot | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `{THEME_TITLE}` | string, 1-2 words ALL CAPS | — | required. May be split across 2 stacked lines (e.g. "SEA" / "ADVENTURE"). |
| `{HERO_SUBJECT}` | string, prose description | — | required. The figure/scene tied to theme. Always rendered photographic, duotone. |
| `{BASE_COLOR}` | string | "deep charcoal" | dark anchor. Pairs with accent. |
| `{ACCENT_COLOR}` | string | theme-appropriate | required. One saturated accent only. Examples: hot coral, ice teal, oxblood crimson, blood red, neon yellow, electric ultramarine. |
| `{ISSUE_NUMBER}` | string | "07" | 2-digit number or short date. |
| `{SUB_CAPTION}` | string, 3-7 words | — | required. Bottom serif-italic tagline. |
| `{MARGIN_TAGLINE}` | string, 3-6 words ALL CAPS | — | required. Vertical small-caps margin copy. |
| `{BADGE_COPY}` | 2-3 short lines, ALL CAPS | — | required. Mid-left badge editorial lines. |
| `{SECONDARY_LANGUAGE_TEXT}` | string, 1-3 glyphs non-Latin | "" | optional. Kanji/cyrillic/etc. flavor. Empty string drops it cleanly. |

## Prompt skeleton

The single coherent prose block to feed `gpt_image_2` at `quality=high`, aspect 2:3:

```
Vertical magazine-cover poster, 2:3 portrait, parametric poster system style — brutalist Swiss editorial meets grunge zine. Massive condensed bold sans-serif display headline "{THEME_TITLE}" (set ALL CAPS, edge-to-edge across the upper third, may stack across two lines if two words). Two-color duotone palette: dark {BASE_COLOR} base plus saturated {ACCENT_COLOR} accent, with cream/ivory text accents only — no third hue.

Hero photograph centered in the mid-frame: {HERO_SUBJECT}. Render the photo as a {ACCENT_COLOR}-and-{BASE_COLOR} duotone with heavy halftone-dot grain and slight CMYK misregistration.

Top-right cluster: large cream "{ISSUE_NUMBER}" with three lines of all-caps editorial micro-copy stacked beside it. Top-left small bar with theme stamp word and a colored dot.

Vertical small-caps margin text reading "{MARGIN_TAGLINE}" running along the right edge in thin condensed sans-serif.

Mid-left secondary badge: solid {ACCENT_COLOR} block containing a stamp-style logo glyph and these three lines of all-caps editorial copy: "{BADGE_COPY}".

Bottom: serif-italic-bold cream sub-caption "{SUB_CAPTION}" set across the lower third. Tiny barcode-style indicator and "ISSUE Nº 07 / VOL. 02" microtext along the bottom strip.

Optional secondary-language flourish "{SECONDARY_LANGUAGE_TEXT}" set as oversized vertical glyph along one margin or as a stamp mark. Drop cleanly if empty.

Whole-canvas grunge treatment: visible film grain, halftone dot pattern, CMYK misregistration, paper-scuff texture, faint dust and scratches. Print-zine fidelity, not clean digital. No watermark, no signature, no QR codes, no price tags, no handle.
```

## Negative cues (append if a generation drifts)

- "no clean vector look, no flat illustration, no smooth gradients"
- "no third color, palette must be strictly two-tone plus cream"
- "no fictional logo wordmarks beyond the badge stamp"
- "no center-justified body paragraphs, only the specified blocks"
- "no extra people in frame beyond the named hero"

presets.template:
# Study Book Covers Template

Derived from the Promptbase listing "Study Book Covers" by @mylab (Midjourney V6.0, paywalled). Reconstructed from 9 public preview images via vision analysis on 2026-06-07. Adapted for **gpt-image-2** via `image-gen-cli` (natural language, no Midjourney `--ar` / `--v` flags).

## Required invariants (verbatim — reproduce in every prompt)

1. **Square 1:1 frame.** Output size 1024×1024 PNG (or engine-native square). Portrait textbook proportions are out of scope unless the user explicitly overrides.
2. **Professional academic study-book / university textbook cover layout.** Polished graphic-design finish suitable for print, not a photo mockup on a physical book.
3. **Central hero illustration** occupying the middle third of the cover — a subject-specific visual that instantly communicates the academic field (3D scientific render, classical engraved illustration, vintage map, anatomical diagram, cybernetic portrait, bold graphic poster art, etc.).
4. **Typography hierarchy with legible rendered text** (no lorem ipsum, no gibberish filler):
   - Small header line at top repeating or introducing the course name.
   - Large bold main title in upper-center or center — serif for humanities/history, clean sans-serif for STEM/tech.
   - Subtitle below the main title in smaller type.
   - Footer band, corner badge, or publisher label with institutional branding ("University", "Science Editorial", "NASA Astronomy", etc.) in small clean type.
5. **Subject-matched color palette** chosen from `references/palettes.md` or user override — the cover's hues must signal the discipline at a glance.
6. **Design accents:** subtle geometric lines, curved dividers between header/footer and artwork, small corner logos or monograms when appropriate — keep layout clean and shelf-ready.
7. **Authoritative educational mood** — modern, print-ready, authoritative, not stock-photo generic.
8. **No watermark, no "@mylab" text, no "MyLab" repeated marks, no PromptBase branding, no QR codes, no price tags.**

## Variable slots

| Slot | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `{SUBJECT}` | string | yes | Academic field — Philosophy, Quantum Physics, Advanced Geometry, Biology, Economics, History, Astronomy, AI, etc. |
| `{MAIN_TITLE}` | string | yes | Primary cover title verbatim — e.g. "PHILOSOPHY", "Advanced Geometry", "Quantum World:" |
| `{SUBTITLE}` | string | yes | Secondary line — e.g. "From Plato to Present", "An Introduction to Astronomy", "Quantum Physics" |
| `{HEADER_LINE}` | string | no | Small top repeat line; default mirrors course name or a shortened variant of `{MAIN_TITLE}` |
| `{HERO_DESCRIPTION}` | prose | yes | One paragraph describing the central illustration style and content for `{SUBJECT}` |
| `{PALETTE_BAND}` | string | no | Named band from `references/palettes.md`; pick mood-matched default if omitted |
| `{PUBLISHER_LABEL}` | string | no | Footer/corner institutional text — e.g. "University", "Science Editorial", "NASA Astronomy" |
| `{TYPOGRAPHY_STYLE}` | enum | no | `serif-humanities` \| `sans-stem` \| `mixed-display`; default from subject |

## Quality-lift directives

Improve execution inside the copied style without drifting to a new art direction.

| Source weakness | Allowed improvement | Style boundary |
|---|---|---|
| MyLab watermarks on every preview | Never reproduce seller watermark or repeated "MyLab" text | Keep academic publisher footer labels the user supplies |
| Occasional mushy 3D edges / plastic AI gloss on STEM covers | Require crisp material separation, plausible lighting, intentional contact shadows on 3D heroes | Same centered hero + STEM palette; no switch to flat vector unless subject calls for it |
| Gibberish or distorted map/type labels on history previews | Require every rendered word to be verbatim from slots; spell uncommon terms letter-by-letter | Same vintage-map / parchment history aesthetic |
| Generic stock-photo feel | Push subject-specific metaphor in `{HERO_DESCRIPTION}` (columns for philosophy, polyhedron for geometry, virus for biology) | Do not change square layout or typography hierarchy |
| Weak footer branding consistency | Use one clear publisher label per cover, sized and placed like a real textbook imprint | Do not add marketing taglines or extra paragraphs of body copy |

## Prompt skeleton

<!-- format: prose, gpt-image-2 -->

```
Professional academic study book cover design for a university {SUBJECT} textbook. Square 1:1 composition, polished graphic-design layout suitable for print.

Central hero illustration: {HERO_DESCRIPTION}. The imagery must instantly communicate {SUBJECT} and dominate the middle third of the cover.

Typography (render all text legibly, no gibberish):
- Top header: "{HEADER_LINE}" in small elegant type matching {TYPOGRAPHY_STYLE}
- Main title: "{MAIN_TITLE}" in very large bold type, centered or upper-center, with subtle drop shadow or outline for readability
- Subtitle: "{SUBTITLE}" in medium type below the main title
- Publisher label: "{PUBLISHER_LABEL}" in small understated type in a footer band or corner badge

Color palette: {PALETTE_BAND} — subject-matched hues that signal the discipline.

Design details: clean centered composition, subtle geometric accents or thin curved dividers separating header/footer from artwork, small corner monogram optional, professional print-ready finish, no watermarks, no stock-photo look. Mood: authoritative, modern, educational, shelf-ready textbook cover.

Style: academic textbook cover, educational publishing, high-resolution graphic design, subject-themed illustration, clean typographic layout.
```

## Validation checklist (run after every generation)

- [ ] Square 1:1 aspect
- [ ] Central subject-specific hero illustration visible
- [ ] `{MAIN_TITLE}` and `{SUBTITLE}` render verbatim and legibly
- [ ] Publisher/footer label present if supplied
- [ ] Palette matches `{SUBJECT}` / `{PALETTE_BAND}`
- [ ] No MyLab / PromptBase / seller watermark
- [ ] Print-ready graphic-design finish (not a photo of a book on a desk)

If 2+ items fail, run one targeted retry naming the failing items. After two retries, surface to the user.

presets.template:
# Foldforge Character Sheet Template

## Required invariants (verbatim — reproduce in every prompt)

1. 2:3 vertical poster sheet. Output size 1024×1536 px (or source aspect when generating to source dimensions).
2. Cream / parchment paper background with subtle paper-grain texture; no pure white.
3. Single hero subject deconstructed into flat papercraft cut-out parts, arranged in three views on the sheet: assembled hero (top center), exploded parts (mid), mid-build view (side or bottom-center). Hero parts occupy ~60% of the canvas height in the upper-middle band.
4. Headline in a chunky slab-serif / geometric-display all-caps font centered at the top, framed by a double-stroke ornamental border. Verbatim slot: `{THEME_TITLE}`.
5. Optional subtitle line directly below the headline in narrow all-caps. Verbatim slot: `{SUBTITLE}` (omit when `{THEME_TITLE}` is 3+ words).
6. Sub-headline below the title block: `CUT • FOLD • ASSEMBLE  —  PAPERCRAFT SET {SET_NUMBER}` in small caps with bullet separators. `{SET_NUMBER}` defaults to `1`.
7. Numbered assembly step strip along the lower-left band: four sequential steps "1 2 3 4" with tiny line-art step glyphs (cut, fold, glue, finish) and one-line captions. Captions are short verbs: `CUT`, `FOLD`, `GLUE`, `DONE` by default; override via `{STEP_CAPTIONS}`.
8. Tools / materials icon strip along the lower-right: scissors, glue stick, ruler, pencil glyphs with small-caps labels. Always present.
9. Tiny finished mini-figure of the hero standing in the bottom-right corner area as a "what it builds into" preview.
10. Strict flat color blocking — no gradients, no photographic shading. 4-5 color palette pulled from `{PALETTE}` plus the cream background unifier. Use the palettes catalog in `palettes.md` or accept a custom 4-5 swatch set.
11. Dotted line "fold-here" indicators rendered inside each cut-out part where folds occur.
12. Double-stroke decorative borders top and bottom of the sheet; small ornamental corner motif drawn from `{CORNER_MOTIF}` (tribal / deco / circuit / leaf / custom).
13. No watermark, no seller signature, no QR codes, no price tags. Explicitly reject "Nasreen703" or any human handle in the rendered output.
14. Text accuracy — quote `{THEME_TITLE}`, `{SUBTITLE}` (if present), the verbatim subhead string, every step caption, and every tool label exactly in the prompt. No invented strings.
15. Editorial poster hierarchy with a 9-cell grid feel: title block (top 1/5), hero composition (middle 3/5), instruction band + tool strip + mini figure (bottom 1/5).

## Variable slots

| Slot | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `{THEME_TITLE}` | string, 1-3 words all caps | — | required |
| `{SUBTITLE}` | string, 1-2 words all caps | empty | optional; auto-omit if title is 3+ words |
| `{HERO_SUBJECT}` | prose, 5-30 words | — | required, describes character/object |
| `{PALETTE}` | enum from palettes.md OR custom 4-5 hex swatches | "desert" | required |
| `{SET_NUMBER}` | integer | 1 | shown in subhead badge |
| `{CORNER_MOTIF}` | enum: tribal / deco / circuit / leaf / custom | matched to palette | optional |
| `{STEP_CAPTIONS}` | array of 4 short verbs | ["CUT","FOLD","GLUE","DONE"] | optional |
| `{ACCENT_TEXTURE}` | enum: none / halftone / paper-fiber / vine | none | optional, single-preview leftovers from source |

## Prompt skeleton

> A 2:3 vertical papercraft cut-and-fold character sheet rendered as a flat-color editorial poster on a cream parchment background with subtle paper-grain texture.
>
> TITLE BLOCK (top fifth): Centered headline "{THEME_TITLE}" in a chunky slab-serif all-caps display font, framed by a double-stroke ornamental border. Subtitle "{SUBTITLE}" centered immediately below in narrow all-caps (omit this line if {SUBTITLE} is empty). Below the title block, a single small-caps subhead reading exactly "CUT • FOLD • ASSEMBLE  —  PAPERCRAFT SET {SET_NUMBER}".
>
> HERO COMPOSITION (middle three-fifths): {HERO_SUBJECT} deconstructed into flat geometric papercraft cut-out parts. Show three arrangements on the sheet: (1) the fully assembled hero standing in a hero pose, (2) the exploded parts laid flat with dotted fold-line indicators inside each piece, (3) a mid-build / partial-assembly view. Use strict flat-color blocking with the {PALETTE} swatch set: 4-5 mood-matched colors plus the cream background unifier. No gradients, no photographic shading. Tiny ornamental icons drawn from the {CORNER_MOTIF} family scattered between parts.
>
> INSTRUCTION BAND (bottom fifth, left): Four sequential numbered assembly steps "1  2  3  4" with tiny line-art step glyphs and short small-caps captions {STEP_CAPTIONS}. Render the numerals as oversized hand-drawn-looking display digits.
>
> TOOLS STRIP (bottom fifth, right): Small-caps row labeled "TOOLS" followed by four flat-icon glyphs of scissors, glue stick, ruler, pencil with the words "SCISSORS", "GLUE", "RULER", "PENCIL" beneath each glyph.
>
> MINI FIGURE: A tiny finished build-preview of the hero standing in the bottom-right corner area as a "this is what you build" thumbnail.
>
> DECORATIONS: Double-stroke decorative borders top and bottom of the sheet. {CORNER_MOTIF} corner ornaments at all four corners. Apply {ACCENT_TEXTURE} sparingly if not "none".
>
> CONSTRAINTS: No watermark. No signature. No human handle. No QR code. No price tag. No real-world brand marks. Render every quoted string exactly as written, no spelling drift. Editorial poster hierarchy, clean 9-cell grid feel, balanced negative space.

The skeleton above is the engine input — fill the slots, then send verbatim to gpt_image_2 at `quality=high`, aspect `2:3`, via Higgsfield primary or imagegen fallback.
